bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第063卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 063
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 63

sentences.zh: 【漢紀五十五】起暑維單閼，盡上章執徐，凡二年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records Fifty-Five】 Beginning from Shuwei-Danyan through Shangzhang-Zhixu—in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 55】 Spanning the years from Shuwei-Danyan through Shangzhang-Zhixu—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，黑山帥張燕與公孫續率兵十萬，三道救之。

translations.literal: In spring, in the third month, the Black Mountain chieftain Zhang Yan and Gongsun Xu led a hundred thousand troops along three routes to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring, the Black Mountain chieftain Zhang Yan and Gongsun Xu marched a hundred thousand men along three routes to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 未至，瓚密使行人繼書告續，使引五千鐵騎於北隰之中，起火為應，瓚欲自內出戰。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Zan secretly sent a messenger with a follow-up letter telling Xu to lead five thousand armored horsemen into the northern lowlands, light fires as a signal, and Zan intended to sally out from within to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Zan secretly sent a courier with a second message instructing Xu to bring five thousand armored cavalry into the northern marshlands and light signal fires; Zan planned to break out from within and join the battle.

sentences.zh: 紹候得其書，如期舉火。

translations.literal: Shao's scouts obtained the letter and lit fires on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's scouts intercepted the message and lit signal fires at the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 瓚以為救至，遂出戰。

translations.literal: Zan thought the relief had arrived and therefore went out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Believing that relief had arrived, Zan sallied out to fight.

sentences.zh: 紹設伏擊之，瓚大敗，復還自守。

translations.literal: Shao set an ambush and struck him; Zan was utterly defeated and withdrew to defend himself again.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had laid an ambush and struck; Zan was routed and retreated once more behind his defenses.

sentences.zh: 紹為地道，穿其樓下，施木柱之，度足達半，便燒之，樓輒傾倒，稍至京中。

translations.literal: Shao dug a tunnel, bored beneath the towers, set up wooden pillars, and when they reached halfway, burned them; the towers then toppled, gradually reaching the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Shao dug a tunnel beneath the towers, propped them with wooden pillars, and when the supports were halfway consumed by fire, burned them; the towers collapsed one after another, the destruction creeping inward toward the citadel.

sentences.zh: 瓚自計必無全，乃悉縊其姊妹、妻子，然後引火自焚。

translations.literal: Zan reckoned that he could not survive intact, so he hanged all his sisters and wives, then set fire and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that he could not escape whole, Zan had all his sisters and wives strangled, then set the fortress ablaze and perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 紹趣兵登台，斬之。

translations.literal: Shao urged his troops onto the platform and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao pressed his troops up onto the platform and had Zan's head taken.

sentences.zh: 田楷戰死。

translations.literal: Tian Kai died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Kai was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 關靖歎曰：「前若不止將軍自行，未必不濟。

translations.literal: Guan Jing sighed and said, "If earlier we had not stopped the general from acting on his own, it might not have failed."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Jing sighed and said, "Had we not earlier restrained the general from acting on his own initiative, the outcome might well have been different."

sentences.zh: 吾聞君子陷人危，必同其難，豈可以獨生乎！

translations.literal: I have heard that when a gentleman plunges others into peril, he must share their hardship—how could he live on alone!
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a gentleman brings others into danger, he must share their fate—how could he save himself alone!"

sentences.zh: 」策馬赴紹軍而死。

translations.literal: " He spurred his horse toward Shao's army and died.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse toward Shao's camp and was killed.

sentences.zh: 續為屠各所殺。

translations.literal: Xu was killed by the Tuge.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was slain by Tuge tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 漁陽田豫說太守鮮于輔曰：「曹氏奉天子以令諸侯，終能定天下，宜早從之。

translations.literal: Tian Yu of Yuyang advised the prefect Xianyu Fu, saying, "The Cao clan holds the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords and will ultimately settle the realm; you ought to submit to them early."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu of Yuyang urged the prefect Xianyu Fu, saying, "The house of Cao holds the emperor to command the lords and will in the end bring the realm to order; you should align yourself with them without delay."

sentences.zh: 」輔乃率其眾以奉王命。

translations.literal: " Fu then led his followers to obey the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Fu thereupon led his followers to submit to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 詔以輔為建忠將軍，都督幽州六郡。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Fu as General Who Establishes Loyalty and superintendent of the six commanderies of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Fu General Who Establishes Loyalty and placed him in command of the six You Province commanderies.

sentences.zh: 初，烏桓王丘力居死，子樓班年少，從子蹋頓有武略，代立，總攝上谷大人難樓、遼東大人蘇僕延、右北平大人烏延等。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wuhuan king Qiuliju died; his son Louban was young, and his nephew Tadun, who had martial prowess, replaced him on the throne and took overall charge of the Shanggu chieftain Nalou, the Liaodong chieftain Supuyan, the Right Beiping chieftain Wuyan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Wuhuan king Qiuliju had died. His son Louban was still young, and his nephew Tadun, a man of military talent, succeeded him and brought under his authority the Shanggu chieftain Nalou, the Liaodong chieftain Supuyan, the Right Beiping chieftain Wuyan, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 袁紹攻公孫瓚，蹋頓以烏桓助之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan, and Tadun aided him with Wuhuan forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao attacked Gongsun Zan, Tadun sent Wuhuan warriors to his aid.

sentences.zh: 瓚滅，紹承製皆賜蹋頓、難樓、蘇僕延、烏延等單于印綬；

translations.literal: After Zan was destroyed, Shao, acting on imperial authority, bestowed on Tadun, Nalou, Supuyan, Wuyan, and the others Chanyu seals and cords;
translations.idiomatic: After Zan's destruction, Shao, acting with imperial sanction, invested Tadun, Nalou, Supuyan, Wuyan, and the others with Chanyu seals and ribbons;

sentences.zh: 又以閻柔得烏桓心，因加寵慰以安北邊。

translations.literal: and because Yan Rou had won the hearts of the Wuhuan, he further showed them favor and consolation to secure the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: and because Yan Rou had won the Wuhuan people's loyalty, he heaped further favor and reassurance upon them to pacify the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 其後難樓、蘇僕延奉樓班為單于，以蹋頓為王，然蹋頓猶秉計策。

translations.literal: Afterward Nalou and Supuyan installed Louban as Chanyu and made Tadun king, yet Tadun still held the planning and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Nalou and Supuyan enthroned Louban as Chanyu and made Tadun king, but Tadun continued to hold real authority over strategy.

sentences.zh: 眭固屯射犬。

translations.literal: Sui Gu garrisoned Shequan.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Gu held Shequan with his troops.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，曹操進軍臨河，使將軍史渙、曹仁渡河擊之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao advanced his army to the riverbank and sent the generals Shi Huan and Cao Ren across the river to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Cao Cao marched to the river and sent the generals Shi Huan and Cao Ren across to strike Sui Gu.

sentences.zh: 仁，操從弟也。

translations.literal: Ren was Cao's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Ren was Cao Cao's cousin.

sentences.zh: 固自將兵北詣袁紹求救，與渙、仁遇於犬城，渙、仁擊斬之。

translations.literal: Gu himself led troops north to seek rescue from Yuan Shao; he encountered Huan and Ren at Quan City, and Huan and Ren attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu himself led his forces north to beg aid from Yuan Shao, but met Huan and Ren at Quan City, where they attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 操遂濟河，圍射犬。

translations.literal: Cao then crossed the river and besieged Shequan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao then crossed the river and laid siege to Shequan.

sentences.zh: 射犬降，操還軍敖倉。

translations.literal: Shequan surrendered, and Cao returned his army to Aocang.
translations.idiomatic: Shequan surrendered, and Cao withdrew his army to Aocang.

sentences.zh: 初，操在兗州舉魏種孝廉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cao was in Yan Province, he nominated Wei Zhong as a filial and incorrupt candidate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Cao Cao was in Yan Province, he had nominated Wei Zhong as a filial and incorrupt candidate.

sentences.zh: 兗州叛，操曰：「唯魏種且不棄孤。

translations.literal: When Yan Province rebelled, Cao said, "Only Wei Zhong would not abandon me."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Province rose in revolt, Cao Cao said, "Only Wei Zhong would not abandon me."

sentences.zh: 」及聞種走，操怒曰：「種不南走越，北走胡，不置汝也！

translations.literal: " When he heard that Zhong had fled, Cao said in anger, "If Zhong does not flee south to Yue or north to the barbarians, I will not let you off!"
translations.idiomatic: But when he learned that Zhong had fled, he raged, "Unless Zhong flees south to Yue or north to the barbarians, I will not spare you!"

sentences.zh: 」即下射犬，生禽種，操曰：「唯其才也！

translations.literal: " He immediately descended on Shequan, captured Zhong alive, and Cao said, "It is only because of his talent!"
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Shequan, took Zhong alive, and said, "I spare you only for your ability!"

sentences.zh: 」釋其縛而用之，以為河內太守，屬以河北事。

translations.literal: " He released his bonds and employed him, making him Administrator of Henei and entrusting him with affairs north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed his bonds and put him to use, appointing him Administrator of Henei and entrusting him with affairs in the Hebei region.

sentences.zh: 以衛將軍董承為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: The Defender-General Dong Cheng was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng, Defender-General, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 袁術既稱帝，淫侈滋甚，媵御數百，無不兼羅紈，厭粱肉，自下饑困，莫之收恤。

translations.literal: After Yuan Shu had declared himself emperor, his debauchery and extravagance grew ever worse; his concubines and attendants numbered in the hundreds, all clad in layered silk gauze and sated with fine grain and meat, while below him the people starved in destitution with no one to gather them in or relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Shu had declared himself emperor, his debauchery and extravagance knew no bounds. His concubines and attendants numbered in the hundreds, every one draped in silk and surfeited with fine grain and meat, while the people below him starved in misery with no one to succor them.

sentences.zh: 既而資實空盡，不能自立，乃燒宮室，奔其部曲陳簡、雷薄於灊山，復為簡等所拒，遂大窮，士卒散走，憂懣不知所為。

translations.literal: Before long his resources and stores were utterly exhausted and he could not sustain himself; he then burned his palaces and fled to his officers Chen Jian and Lei Bo on Qian Mountain, but was again rejected by Jian and the others, and so fell into utter destitution; his soldiers scattered and fled, and he was anguished and at a loss as to what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his stores were exhausted and he could no longer hold his own. He burned his palaces and fled to his officers Chen Jian and Lei Bo on Mount Qian, only to be turned away by them as well. Reduced to utter ruin, his troops scattered, and he was consumed by despair with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使歸帝號於從兄紹曰：「祿去漢室久矣！

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to return the imperial title to his cousin Shao, saying, "The Mandate has long departed from the house of Han!"
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to surrender the imperial title to his cousin Yuan Shao, saying, "The Mandate has long since left the house of Han!"

sentences.zh: 袁氏受命當王，符瑞炳然。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan has received the Mandate and ought to become king; the omens and portents blaze forth.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Yuan has received Heaven's charge and is destined to rule; the omens blaze clear.

sentences.zh: 今君擁有四州，人戶百萬，謹歸大命，君其興之！

translations.literal: Now you hold four provinces and a million households; I respectfully return the Great Mandate—may you rise to it!
translations.idiomatic: You now hold four provinces and a million households. I respectfully return the Great Mandate to you—may you rise to claim it!"

sentences.zh: 」袁譚自青州迎術，欲從下邳北過。

translations.literal: " Yuan Tan came from Qing Province to welcome Shu and intended to pass north from Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan came from Qing Province to receive Shu and planned to lead him north past Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 曹操遣劉備及將軍清河朱靈邀之，術不得過，復走壽春。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent Liu Bei and the Qinghe general Zhu Ling to intercept him; Shu could not pass through and fled back to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Liu Bei and the Qinghe general Zhu Ling to block his path. Shu could not get through and retreated once more to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 六月，至江亭，坐簀床而歎曰：「袁術乃至是乎！

translations.literal: In the sixth month he reached Jiangting, sat on a bamboo couch, and sighed, saying, "Has Yuan Shu really come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he reached Jiang Pavilion, sat on a rush mat, and sighed, "Has Yuan Shu truly come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」因憤慨結病，歐血死。

translations.literal: " He then, from indignant rage, developed an illness, vomited blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rage and grief took hold of him; he fell ill, vomited blood, and died.

sentences.zh: 術從弟胤畏曹操，不敢居壽春，率其部曲奉術柩及妻子，奔廬江太守劉勳於皖城。

translations.literal: Shu's cousin Yin feared Cao Cao and dared not remain in Shouchun; he led his followers, bearing Shu's coffin and wives, and fled to the Lujiang Administrator Liu Xun at Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's cousin Yin, fearing Cao Cao, dared not remain in Shouchun. He led his followers, bearing Shu's coffin and family, and fled to the Lujiang administrator Liu Xun at Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 故廣陵太守徐璆得傳國璽。

translations.literal: The former Guangling Administrator Xu Miao obtained the imperial heirloom seal.
translations.idiomatic: The former Guangling administrator Xu Miao came into possession of the imperial heirloom seal.

sentences.zh: 獻之。

translations.literal: He presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He presented it to the court.

sentences.zh: 袁紹既克公孫瓚，心益驕，貢御稀簡。

translations.literal: After Yuan Shao had conquered Gongsun Zan, his heart grew ever prouder, and his tribute to the court grew sparse and perfunctory.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shao had overthrown Gongsun Zan, his pride swelled, and the tribute he sent to the court grew sparse and perfunctory.

sentences.zh: 主薄耿包密白紹，宜應天人，稱尊號。

translations.literal: The chief clerk Geng Bao secretly advised Shao that he ought to respond to Heaven and the people and assume the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk Geng Bao secretly urged Shao to heed Heaven and the people and assume the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 紹以包白事示軍府。

translations.literal: Shao displayed Bao's private report to the military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shao made Bao's proposal known throughout his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 僚屬皆言包妖妄，宜誅。

translations.literal: The staff all said Bao was deluded and perverse and ought to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: His staff all declared that Bao was deluded and perverse and ought to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 紹不得已，殺包以自解。

translations.literal: Shao had no choice but to kill Bao to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had no choice but to execute Bao to clear himself of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 紹簡精兵十萬、騎萬匹，欲以攻許。

translations.literal: Shao selected a hundred thousand elite troops and ten thousand horsemen and intended to attack Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao mustered a hundred thousand picked troops and ten thousand cavalry and prepared to march on Xu.

sentences.zh: 沮授諫曰：「近討公孫瓚，師出歷年，百姓疲敝，倉庫無積，未可動也。

translations.literal: Ju Shou remonstrated, saying, "In the recent campaign against Gongsun Zan the army was in the field for years; the people are exhausted and depleted, the storehouses have no accumulations—it is not yet possible to move."
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou remonstrated, saying, "The recent campaign against Gongsun Zan kept the army in the field for years. The people are exhausted, the storehouses empty—it is not yet time to march."

sentences.zh: 宜務農息民，先遣使獻捷天子。

translations.literal: You ought to devote yourself to agriculture and give the people rest, and first send envoys to present your victory to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: You should devote yourself to farming and give the people rest, and first send envoys to present your victory to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 若不得通，乃表曹操隔我王路，然後進屯黎陽，漸營河南，益作舟舡，繕修器械，分遣精騎抄其邊鄙，令彼不得安，我取其逸。

translations.literal: If you cannot get through, then memorialize that Cao Cao is blocking our royal road; afterward advance and encamp at Liyang, gradually develop the Henan region, increase the building of boats, repair weapons, and dispatch elite cavalry in detachments to raid his borderlands, so that he cannot be at ease while we take our ease—
translations.idiomatic: If they are turned back, then memorialize that Cao Cao is blocking the royal road. Only then advance to encamp at Liyang, gradually develop the Henan region, build more boats, repair weapons, and dispatch elite cavalry in detachments to raid his borders, keeping him unsettled while we remain at ease—

sentences.zh: 如此，可坐定也。

translations.literal: in this way you can settle the realm while seated.
translations.idiomatic: and in this way you can bring the realm to order without stirring from your seat."

sentences.zh: 」郭圖、審配曰：「以明公之神武，引河朔之強眾，以伐曹操，易如覆手，何必乃爾！

translations.literal: " Guo Tu and Shen Pei said, "With my lord's divine martial prowess, leading the mighty hosts of the Yellow River north to attack Cao Cao—it is as easy as turning the hand over; why must it be thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu and Shen Pei said, "With my lord's divine martial prowess, leading the mighty hosts of Hebei against Cao Cao, victory is as easy as turning one's hand—why make it so complicated!"

sentences.zh: 」授曰：「夫救亂誅暴，謂之義兵；

translations.literal: " Shou said, "Troops that rescue disorder and punish violence are called righteous armies;
translations.idiomatic: Shou replied, "Armies that rescue the realm from chaos and punish the violent are called armies of righteousness;

sentences.zh: 恃眾憑強，謂之驕兵。

translations.literal: those that rely on numbers and lean on strength are called arrogant armies.
translations.idiomatic: those that lean on numbers and trust in brute strength are called arrogant armies.

sentences.zh: 義者無敵，驕者先滅。

translations.literal: The righteous have no enemy; the arrogant perish first.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous are invincible; the arrogant are the first to fall.

sentences.zh: 曹操奉天子以令天下，今舉師南向，於義則違。

translations.literal: Cao Cao holds the Son of Heaven to command the realm; if you now raise an army southward, in righteousness you violate the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao holds the emperor to command the realm. To march south now is to violate righteousness itself.

sentences.zh: 且廟勝之策，不在強弱。

translations.literal: Moreover, strategies that win in the ancestral temple do not depend on strength or weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, victory decided in the ancestral temple does not depend on numbers alone.

sentences.zh: 曹操法令既行，士卒精練，非公孫瓚坐而受攻者也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's laws and orders are already enforced, his soldiers drilled and honed—they are not like Gongsun Zan, who sat and received attack.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's laws are enforced, his troops drilled and disciplined—he is not Gongsun Zan, who sat passively and took whatever blows came.

sentences.zh: 今棄萬安之術而興無名之師，竊為公懼之！

translations.literal: Now you abandon ten-thousand-fold secure tactics and raise an army without a name—I privately fear for you!
translations.idiomatic: To abandon a sure path and raise an army without just cause—I fear for you, my lord!"

sentences.zh: 」圖、配曰：「武王伐紂，不為不義。

translations.literal: " Tu and Pei said, "King Wu attacked King Zhou—was that not righteous?
translations.idiomatic: Tu and Pei said, "When King Wu attacked King Zhou of Shang, was that unrighteous?

sentences.zh: 況兵加曹操，而云無名？

translations.literal: How much less when you send troops against Cao Cao can you say it is without a name?
translations.idiomatic: How much less so when you send troops against Cao Cao—how can you call that unjustified?

sentences.zh: 且以公今日之強，將士思奮，不及時以定大業，所謂天與不取，反受其咎，此越之所以霸，吳之所以滅也。

translations.literal: Moreover, with my lord's strength today, officers and soldiers eager to fight—if you do not seize the moment to settle the great enterprise, it is what is called Heaven gives and you do not take, then turn and receive its punishment; this is why Yue achieved hegemony and Wu was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with your strength today and your officers eager to fight, if you do not seize the moment to secure the great enterprise, you will suffer what Heaven offers and man refuses—the fate that made Yue a hegemon and Wu a ruin."

sentences.zh: 監軍之計在於持牢，而非見時知機之變也。

translations.literal: The army supervisor's plan lies in holding firm, not in perceiving the times and knowing how opportunity shifts.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor's plan is to hold fast, not to read the times and seize opportunity."

sentences.zh: 」紹納圖言，圖等因是譖授曰：「授監統內外，威震三軍，若其浸盛，何以制之！

translations.literal: " Shao accepted Tu's words; Tu and the others therefore slandered Shou, saying, "Shou supervises and commands inside and outside; his authority shakes the three armies—if it gradually grows great, how will you control him!"
translations.idiomatic: Shao accepted Tu's counsel. Tu and his allies then slandered Shou, saying, "Shou commands both civil and military affairs; his authority overawes the entire army. If it keeps growing, how will you control him?"

sentences.zh: 夫臣與主同者亡，此《黃石》之所忌也。

translations.literal: When minister and lord are alike, destruction follows—this is what the Yellow Stone Classic warns against.
translations.idiomatic: When minister and lord are equals, ruin follows—this is what the Yellow Stone Classic warns against.

sentences.zh: 且御眾於外，不宜知內。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who commands the masses outside ought not to know the inner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a commander in the field should not know too much of what happens within."

sentences.zh: 」紹乃分授所統為三都督，使授及郭圖、淳于瓊各典一軍。

translations.literal: " Shao then divided what Shou commanded into three command areas and had Shou, Guo Tu, and Chunyu Qiong each administer one army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then split Shou's command into three divisions, placing Shou, Guo Tu, and Chunyu Qiong each in charge of one army.

sentences.zh: 騎都尉清河崔琰諫曰：「天子在許，民望助順，不可攻也！

translations.literal: The Cavalry Commandant Cui Yan of Qinghe remonstrated, saying, "The Son of Heaven is at Xu; the people look to those who aid the righteous—he must not be attacked!"
translations.idiomatic: The Cavalry Commandant Cui Yan of Qinghe remonstrated, saying, "The emperor is at Xu; the people look to whoever aids the legitimate cause—you must not attack!"

sentences.zh: 」紹不從。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Shao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 許下諸將聞紹將攻許，皆懼，曹操曰：「吾知紹之為人，志大而智小，色厲而膽薄，忌克而少威，兵多而分畫不明，將驕而政令不一，土地雖廣，糧食雖豐，適足以為吾奉也。

translations.literal: The generals at Xu, hearing that Shao was about to attack Xu, were all afraid; Cao Cao said, "I know Shao's character: great in ambition but small in wisdom, fierce in appearance but thin in courage, jealous and grasping with little authority, many in troops but unclear in division of plans, generals arrogant and government orders not unified—though his lands are broad and his grain abundant, they will serve only as provisions for me."
translations.idiomatic: When the generals at Xu heard that Shao was marching on the capital, they were all afraid. Cao Cao said, "I know Shao's character: ambitious but shallow in counsel, fierce in manner but timid at heart, jealous and grasping with little real authority, many in troops but muddled in planning, his generals arrogant and his orders inconsistent. However broad his lands and however full his granaries, they will serve only to provision me."

sentences.zh: 」孔融謂荀彧曰：「紹地廣兵強，田豐、許攸智士也，為之謀；

translations.literal: " Kong Rong said to Xun Yu, "Shao's territory is broad and his troops strong; Tian Feng and Xu You are wise men who plan for him;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong said to Xun Yu, "Shao's territory is vast and his army strong. Tian Feng and Xu You are wise counselors who plot for him;

sentences.zh: 審配、逄紀忠臣也，任其事；

translations.literal: Shen Pei and Pang Ji are loyal ministers who undertake his affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei and Pang Ji are loyal ministers who carry out his orders;

sentences.zh: 顏良、文丑勇將也，統其兵。

translations.literal: Yan Liang and Wen Chou are brave generals who command his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Liang and Wen Chou are fierce generals who lead his armies.

sentences.zh: 殆難克乎！

translations.literal: He will be hard to overcome, will he not!"
translations.idiomatic: He will be hard to overcome, will he not?"

sentences.zh: 」彧曰：「紹兵雖多而法不整，田豐剛而犯上，許攸貪而不治，審配專而無謀，逄紀果而自用，此數人者，勢不相容，必生內變。

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Though Shao's troops are many, his methods are not orderly; Tian Feng is obstinate and offends his superiors, Xu You is greedy and does not govern well, Shen Pei is domineering and without strategy, Pang Ji is decisive but self-willed—these several men cannot coexist in power and will surely produce internal strife.
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "Shao's troops are numerous but his discipline is lax. Tian Feng is obstinate and offends his superiors; Xu You is greedy and corrupt; Shen Pei is domineering and unstrategic; Pang Ji is headstrong and self-willed. These men cannot coexist in power—they will surely tear one another apart.

sentences.zh: 顏良、文丑，一夫之勇耳，可一戰而禽也。

translations.literal: Yan Liang and Wen Chou are merely the courage of a single man—they can be captured in one battle."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Liang and Wen Chou are mere brawlers—they can be taken in a single engagement."

sentences.zh: 」秋，八月，操進軍黎陽，使臧霸等將精兵入青州以扞東方，留于禁屯河上。

translations.literal: " In autumn, in the eighth month, Cao advanced his army to Liyang, sent Zang Ba and others to lead elite troops into Qing Province to block the east, and left Yu Jin to garrison on the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, Cao advanced to Liyang, sent Zang Ba and others with elite troops into Qing Province to hold the eastern flank, and left Yu Jin to garrison along the river.

sentences.zh: 九月，操還許，分兵守官渡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Cao returned to Xu and divided troops to guard Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Cao returned to Xu and detached troops to hold Guandu.

sentences.zh: 袁紹遣人招張繡，並與賈詡書結好。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao sent men to recruit Zhang Xiu and also sent Jia Xu a letter to form friendly ties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent envoys to win over Zhang Xiu and wrote Jia Xu a letter offering alliance.

sentences.zh: 繡欲許之，詡於繡坐上，顯謂紹使曰：「歸謝袁本初，兄弟不能相容，而能容天下國士乎！

translations.literal: Xiu was about to agree; Xu, in Xiu's presence at his seat, said openly to Shao's envoy, "Go back and thank Yuan Benchu: brothers cannot tolerate each other—how could he accommodate the outstanding men of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was inclined to accept. At the council table, Xu said openly to Shao's envoy, "Go back and tell Yuan Benchu this: brothers cannot abide one another—how could he make room for the finest men of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」繡驚懼曰：「何至於此！

translations.literal: " Xiu was startled and afraid, saying, "How could it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was startled and alarmed. "How could you go so far!" he said.

sentences.zh: 」竊謂詡曰：「若此，當何歸？

translations.literal: " He said privately to Xu, "If it is thus, where ought we to go?"
translations.idiomatic: He drew Xu aside and asked, "If that is how things stand, where should we turn?"

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「不如從曹公。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "It would be better to follow Lord Cao."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "Better to follow Lord Cao."

sentences.zh: 」繡曰：「袁強曹弱，又先與曹為仇，從之如何？

translations.literal: " Xiu said, "Yuan is strong and Cao weak, and moreover we were enemies with Cao first—how could we follow him?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "Yuan is strong and Cao weak, and we were Cao's enemies first—how could we submit to him?"

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「此乃所以宜從也。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "This is precisely why it is fitting to follow him."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "That is precisely why you should follow him."

sentences.zh: 夫曹公奉天子以令天下，其宜從一也；

translations.literal: Lord Cao holds the Son of Heaven to command the realm—this is the first reason it is fitting to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao holds the emperor to command the realm—that is the first reason to follow him;

sentences.zh: 紹強盛，我以少眾從之，必不以我為重，曹公眾弱，其得我必喜，其宜從二也；

translations.literal: Yuan is powerful and flourishing—if we follow him with few troops, he will surely not regard us as important; Lord Cao's forces are few and weak—when he obtains us he will surely be delighted; this is the second reason it is fitting to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan is powerful—if we join him with a small force, he will never value us highly; Lord Cao's forces are few—when he gains us he will surely be delighted. That is the second reason;

sentences.zh: 夫有霸王之志者，固將釋私怨以明德於四海，其宜從三也。

translations.literal: one who has the ambition of a hegemon-king will surely release private enmities to display virtue to the four seas—this is the third reason it is fitting to follow.
translations.idiomatic: a man with the ambition of a hegemon will set aside private grudges to show his virtue to the realm—that is the third reason.

sentences.zh: 願將軍無疑！

translations.literal: I hope the general will have no doubts!
translations.idiomatic: I urge you, General, to have no doubts!"

sentences.zh: 」冬，十一月，繡率眾降曹操，操執繡手，與歡宴，為子均取繡女，拜揚武將軍；

translations.literal: " In winter, in the eleventh month, Xiu led his followers to surrender to Cao Cao; Cao took Xiu's hand and feasted with him in joy, had his son Jun take Xiu's daughter in marriage, and appointed him General Who Displays Martiality;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, Xiu led his followers to surrender to Cao Cao. Cao took his hand and feasted with him in celebration, betrothed his son Jun to Xiu's daughter, and appointed him General Who Displays Martiality;

sentences.zh: 表詡為執金吾，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: he memorialized Xu as Bearer of the Mace and enfeoffed him as Marquis of the Capital Precinct.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Xu Bearer of the Mace and enfeoffed him as Marquis of the Capital Precinct.

sentences.zh: 關中諸將以袁、曹方爭，皆中立顧望。

translations.literal: The generals of Guanzhong, because Yuan and Cao were contending, all remained neutral and looked on.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong generals, seeing Yuan and Cao locked in conflict, all held neutral and waited to see which way fortune turned.

sentences.zh: 涼州牧韋端使從事天水楊阜詣許，阜還，關右諸將問：「袁、曹勝敗孰在？

translations.literal: The Liangzhou Governor Wei Duan sent his aide Yang Fu of Tianshui to visit Xu; when Fu returned, the generals of the Guanxi region asked, "Between Yuan and Cao, who will win and who will lose?"
translations.idiomatic: The Liangzhou governor Wei Duan sent his aide Yang Fu of Tianshui to visit Xu. When Fu returned, the Guanxi generals asked him, "Between Yuan and Cao, who will prevail?"

sentences.zh: 」阜曰：「袁公寬而不斷，好謀而少決；

translations.literal: " Fu said, "Lord Yuan is generous but not decisive, fond of planning but short on resolution;
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Lord Yuan is generous but indecisive, fond of counsel but slow to act;

sentences.zh: 不斷則無威，少決則後事，今雖強，終不能成大業。

translations.literal: Without decisiveness there is no authority; with little resolution affairs lag behind—though strong now, in the end he cannot accomplish the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Without decisiveness he lacks authority; with too little resolution he lets affairs drift. However strong he is today, he will never complete the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 曹公有雄才遠略，決機無疑，法一而兵精，能用度外之人，所任各盡其力，必能濟大事者也。

translations.literal: Lord Cao has heroic talent and far-reaching strategy, decides opportunities without doubt, unifies laws and has honed troops, can employ men beyond ordinary measure, and those he appoints each exhaust their strength—he will surely be able to accomplish the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao has heroic talent and far-reaching strategy, acts without hesitation, unifies his laws and fields a honed army, and can employ extraordinary men who give their all in his service. He will surely bring the great enterprise to completion.

sentences.zh: 」曹操使治書待御史河東衛覬鎮撫關中，時四方大有還民，關中諸將多引為部曲。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao sent the Imperial Clerk and Attending Censor Wei Ji of Hedong to pacify Guanzhong; at the time people were returning in great numbers from all directions, and the Guanzhong generals mostly recruited them as personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent the imperial clerk and attending censor Wei Ji of Hedong to pacify Guanzhong. Refugees were streaming home from every quarter, and the Guanzhong generals were recruiting them as private retainers.

sentences.zh: 覬書與荀彧：「關中膏腴之地，頃遭荒亂，人民流入荊州者十萬餘家，聞本土安寧，皆企望思歸。

translations.literal: Ji wrote to Xun Yu: "Guanzhong is a fertile land; it has recently suffered wild disorder, and more than a hundred thousand households of people have flowed into Jing Province. Hearing that their homeland is at peace, they all look longingly and think of returning.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote to Xun Yu: "Guanzhong is rich land that has lately been ravaged by chaos. More than a hundred thousand households fled into Jing Province, and now that they hear their homeland is secure, they yearn to return.

sentences.zh: 而歸者無以自業，諸將各競招懷以為部曲，郡縣貧弱，不能與爭，兵家遂強，一旦變動，必有後憂。

translations.literal: Yet those who return have no means to support themselves; the generals each compete to recruit and cherish them as personal troops, while the commanderies and counties are poor and weak and cannot contend with them—the military families grow strong, and if there is a sudden change, there will surely be trouble afterward.
translations.idiomatic: But the returnees have no livelihood. The generals compete to recruit them as retainers, while the counties are too poor and weak to resist. The military clans grow ever stronger, and if trouble erupts, the consequences will be grave.

sentences.zh: 夫鹽，國之大寶也，亂來放散，宜如舊置使者監賣，以其直益市犁牛，若有歸民，以供給之，勤耕積粟以豐殖關中，遠民聞之，必日夜競還。

translations.literal: Salt is a great treasure of the state; since the disorder it has been scattered and released—it is fitting to restore envoys to supervise its sale as before, use the proceeds to buy more plow oxen in the markets, and if there are returning people, supply them, urging diligent farming and accumulating grain to enrich Guanzhong; distant people hearing of this will surely race back day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Salt is one of the state's great treasures. Since the chaos it has been left unregulated. We should restore imperial agents to supervise its sale as before, use the revenue to buy plow oxen, and supply returning settlers so they can farm diligently and fill the granaries of Guanzhong. When distant refugees hear of this, they will rush home without pause.

sentences.zh: 又使司隸校尉留治關中以為之主，則諸將日削，官民日盛，此強本弱敵之利也。

translations.literal: Further, have the Director of Retainers remain to govern Guanzhong as its master—then the generals will daily be reduced and officials and people daily flourish; this is the advantage of strengthening the root and weakening the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Station the Director of Retainers in Guanzhong as the supreme authority, and the generals will daily lose power while the civil administration grows. That is how we strengthen our foundation and weaken our foes.

sentences.zh: 」彧以白操，操從之。

translations.literal: " Yu reported this to Cao, and Cao followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported this to Cao Cao, who adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 始遣謁者僕射監鹽官，司隸校尉治弘農。

translations.literal: He first sent the Master of Ceremonies to supervise the salt officials, and the Director of Retainers governed Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the Master of Ceremonies to oversee the salt monopoly and stationed the Director of Retainers at Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 關中由是服從。

translations.literal: Guanzhong thereby submitted in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong thereupon submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 袁紹使人求助於劉表，表許之而竟不至，亦不援曹操。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao sent men to seek aid from Liu Biao; Biao promised but in the end did not come, nor did he aid Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent envoys to beg aid from Liu Biao. Biao promised help but never came, and he did not aid Cao Cao either.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎南陽韓嵩、別駕零陵劉先說表曰：「今兩雄相持，天下之重在於將軍。

translations.literal: The Attendant Gentleman Han Song of Nanyang and the Separate-Chariot Administrator Liu Xian of Lingling said to Biao, "Now the two mighty ones are locked in stalemate—the weight of the realm lies with the general."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant gentleman Han Song of Nanyang and the separate-chariot administrator Liu Xian of Lingling urged Biao, saying, "The two great powers are locked in stalemate, and the fate of the realm rests with you, General."

sentences.zh: 若欲有為。

translations.literal: If you wish to act,
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to act on your own,

sentences.zh: 起乘其敝可也；

translations.literal: rise and seize their exhaustion—you may succeed;
translations.idiomatic: rise now and strike while they are exhausted;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，固將擇所宜從。

translations.literal: if it is not so, you must surely choose whom it is fitting to follow.
translations.idiomatic: if not, you must choose which side to join.

sentences.zh: 豈可擁甲十萬，坐觀成敗，求援而不能助，見賢而不肯歸。

translations.literal: How could you hold a hundred thousand armored troops, sit and watch success or failure, seek aid yet be unable to help, see the worthy yet be unwilling to submit?
translations.idiomatic: How can you hold a hundred thousand armored troops, sit idle while the contest is decided, fail to answer a plea for aid, and refuse to align yourself with the worthy?

sentences.zh: 此兩怨必集於將軍，恐不得中立矣。

translations.literal: These two resentments will surely gather on the general—I fear you will not be able to remain neutral.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides will surely turn their resentment upon you, and you will not be able to remain neutral.

sentences.zh: 曹操善用兵，賢俊多歸之，其勢必舉袁紹，然後移兵以向江、漢，恐將軍不能御也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao is skilled in using troops; worthy and outstanding men mostly go to him—his momentum will surely overcome Yuan Shao, and afterward he will shift his army toward the Yangzi and Han rivers; I fear the general will not be able to withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao is a master of war, and the finest men flock to him. He will surely overcome Yuan Shao and then turn his armies toward the Yangzi and Han. I fear you will not be able to withstand him.

sentences.zh: 今之勝計，莫若舉荊州以附曹操，操必重德將軍。

translations.literal: Of winning plans today, none surpasses offering Jing Province to attach yourself to Cao Cao—Cao will surely heavily honor the general.
translations.idiomatic: The surest course now is to offer Jing Province to Cao Cao. He will surely reward you richly.

sentences.zh: 長享福祚。

translations.literal: You will long enjoy fortune and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: You and your heirs will enjoy lasting prosperity.

sentences.zh: 垂之後嗣，此萬全之策也。

translations.literal: It will extend to later descendants—this is the ten-thousand-fold secure stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Your descendants will reap the benefit. That is the surest strategy of all."

sentences.zh: 」蒯越亦勸之。

translations.literal: " Kuai Yue also urged him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Yue urged the same course.

sentences.zh: 表狐疑不斷，乃遣嵩詣許，曰：「今天下未知所定，而曹操擁天子都許，君為我觀其釁。

translations.literal: Biao was hesitant and indecisive and therefore sent Song to Xu, saying, "Today the realm does not yet know what will be settled, while Cao Cao holds the Son of Heaven and has his capital at Xu—go observe his openings for me."
translations.idiomatic: Biao, hesitant and unable to decide, sent Song to Xu, saying, "The realm's outcome is still uncertain. Cao Cao holds the emperor at Xu—go observe his intentions for me."

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「聖達節，次守節。

translations.literal: " Song said, "The sage attains to integrity; next is to guard integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "The sage attains to integrity; next comes guarding integrity.

sentences.zh: 嵩，守節者也。

translations.literal: Song is one who guards integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I, Song, am one who guards integrity.

sentences.zh: 夫君臣名定，以死守之。

translations.literal: When lord and minister names are fixed, one guards them unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When the bond between lord and minister is fixed, one defends it unto death.

sentences.zh: 今策名委質，唯將軍所命，雖赴湯蹈火，死無辭也。

translations.literal: Now my name is registered and my substance entrusted—only the general commands; though I enter boiling water or tread fire, I die without refusal.
translations.idiomatic: I have pledged my name and entrusted my person to you and obey only your command. Though I walk through fire, I will not refuse.

sentences.zh: 以嵩觀之，曹公必得志於天下。

translations.literal: As Song sees it, Lord Cao will surely achieve his aim in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, Lord Cao will surely prevail over the realm.

sentences.zh: 將軍能上順天子，下歸曹公，使嵩可也；

translations.literal: If the general can above follow the Son of Heaven and below submit to Lord Cao, then Song may go;
translations.idiomatic: If you, General, will follow the emperor above and submit to Lord Cao below, I may go;

sentences.zh: 如其猶豫，嵩至京師，天子假嵩一職，不獲辭命，則成天子之臣，將軍之故吏耳。

translations.literal: if you still hesitate, when Song reaches the capital the Son of Heaven will lend Song one office—I cannot decline the command—then I become the Son of Heaven's minister, merely the general's former subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: but if you still hesitate, once I reach the capital the emperor will grant me an office I cannot refuse, and I will become the emperor's minister—no longer your servant in any binding sense.

sentences.zh: 在君為君，則嵩守天子之命，義不得復為將軍死也。

translations.literal: When with a lord one is a subject, then Song must guard the Son of Heaven's command—in righteousness I cannot again die for the general.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty follows the throne: I would then owe my duty to the emperor and could not die for you, General.

sentences.zh: 惟加重思，無為負嵩！

translations.literal: Only ponder this deeply—do not wrong Song!
translations.idiomatic: Think on this carefully, and do not place me in an impossible position!"

sentences.zh: 」表以為憚使，強之。

translations.literal: " Biao thought he feared the mission and forced him to go.
translations.idiomatic: Biao thought Song was merely afraid and compelled him to go.

sentences.zh: 至許，詔拜嵩侍中、零陵太守。

translations.literal: When he reached Xu, an edict appointed Song Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Administrator of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: At Xu an edict appointed Song Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Administrator of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 及還，盛稱朝廷、曹公之德，勸表遣子入侍。

translations.literal: When he returned, he lavishly praised the court and Lord Cao's virtue and urged Biao to send his son to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he lavishly praised the court and Lord Cao's virtue and urged Biao to send his son to attend at court.

sentences.zh: 表大怒，以為懷貳，大會寮屬，陳兵，持節，將斬之，數曰：「韓嵩敢懷貳邪！

translations.literal: Biao was greatly enraged, thinking he harbored divided loyalty; he convened a great assembly of his staff, arrayed troops, held the staff of authority, and was about to behead him, saying repeatedly, "Han Song dares to harbor divided loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Biao flew into a rage, believing Song had turned disloyal. He convened his staff, arrayed troops, took up the staff of authority, and was about to execute him, crying, "Does Han Song dare to play the traitor?"

sentences.zh: 」眾皆恐，欲令嵩謝，嵩不為動容，徐謂表曰：「將軍負嵩，嵩不負將軍！

translations.literal: " All were afraid and wanted Song to apologize; Song did not change expression and said calmly to Biao, "The general has wronged Song—Song has not wronged the general!"
translations.idiomatic: The assembly was terrified and urged Song to apologize. Song did not flinch and said calmly, "You have wronged me, General—I have not wronged you!"

sentences.zh: 」且陳前言。

translations.literal: " He then set forth his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: He then repeated what he had said before his departure.

sentences.zh: 表妻蔡氏諫曰：「韓嵩，楚國之望也；

translations.literal: Biao's wife, Lady Cai, remonstrated, saying, "Han Song is the hope of the Chu region;
translations.idiomatic: Biao's wife, Lady Cai, remonstrated, saying, "Han Song is a man the Chu region looks up to;

sentences.zh: 且其言直，誅之無辭。

translations.literal: moreover his words are straight—to execute him there is no justification.
translations.idiomatic: and his words are honest. To kill him would be unjustifiable."

sentences.zh: 」表猶怒，考殺從行者，知無它意，乃弗誅而囚之。

translations.literal: " Biao was still angry, examined and killed those who had accompanied him, and knowing there was no other intent, then did not execute Song but imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was still angry. He tortured and killed Song's attendants, and finding no evidence of treachery, spared Song but imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 揚州賊帥鄭寶欲略居民以赴江表，以淮南劉曄，高族名人，欲劫之使唱此謀，曄患之。

translations.literal: The Yang Province bandit chieftain Zheng Bao wished to plunder the inhabitants to go to the lands south of the Yangzi; because Liu Ye of Huainan was a man of eminent clan and famous name, he wanted to seize him to proclaim this plan—Ye was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang Province bandit chieftain Zheng Bao planned to plunder the populace and flee south of the Yangzi. He wanted to seize Liu Ye of Huainan, a man of eminent lineage, and force him to lead the scheme. Ye was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 會曹操遣使詣州，有所案問，曄要與歸家，寶來候使者，曄留與宴飲，手刃殺之，斬其首以令寶軍曰「曹公有令，敢有動者，與寶同罪！

translations.literal: It happened that Cao Cao sent an envoy to the province on some investigation; Ye asked to return home with him. Bao came to visit the envoy; Ye detained him for a feast and drinking, killed him with his own hand, and cut off his head to command Bao's army, saying, "Lord Cao has an order—whoever dares move shares Bao's crime!"
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao sent an envoy to the province on official business, Ye asked to accompany him home. Bao came to call on the envoy. Ye detained him for a feast, killed him with his own hand, and displayed the severed head before Bao's troops, proclaiming, "Lord Cao has decreed: whoever moves shall share Bao's guilt!"

sentences.zh: 」其眾數千人皆龍言服，推曄為主。

translations.literal: " His followers, several thousand, all submitted in silence and made Ye their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand men submitted in silence and made Ye their leader.

sentences.zh: 曄以其眾與廬江太守劉勳，勳怪其故，曄曰：「寶無法制，其眾素以鈔略為利。

translations.literal: Ye gave these followers to the Lujiang Administrator Liu Xun; Xun wondered at the reason. Ye said, "Bao had no laws or regulations; his followers were accustomed to taking plunder as profit.
translations.idiomatic: Ye handed the force over to the Lujiang administrator Liu Xun. When Xun asked why, Ye said, "Bao had no discipline, and his men lived by plunder.

sentences.zh: 僕宿無資，而整齊之，必懷怨難久，故以相與耳！

translations.literal: I have long had no resources, yet if I put them in order they will surely harbor resentment and be hard to keep long—so I give them to you!"
translations.idiomatic: I have no means to support them, and if I tried to discipline them they would resent me and not stay. That is why I give them to you!"

sentences.zh: 」勳以袁術部典眾多，不能贍，遣從弟偕求米於上繚諸宗帥，不能滿數，偕召勳使襲之。

translations.literal: " Xun, because Yuan Shu's former troops and retainers were numerous and he could not support them, sent his younger cousin Jie to seek grain from the clan chieftains of Shangliao but could not obtain the full amount; Jie summoned Xun to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, unable to feed Yuan Shu's former troops in his service, sent his cousin Jie to beg grain from the Shangliao clan chieftains. When they failed to supply the full amount, Jie urged Xun to attack them.

sentences.zh: 孫策惡勳兵強，偽卑辭以事勳曰：「上繚宗民數欺鄙郡，欲擊之，路不便。

translations.literal: Sun Ce hated that Xun's troops were strong and with false humble words addressed Xun, saying, "The Shangliao clansmen have repeatedly bullied my humble commandery; I wish to strike them, but the route is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce, alarmed by Xun's growing strength, addressed him with feigned humility: "The Shangliao clans have repeatedly harassed my territory, and I wish to strike them, but the route is inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 上繚甚富實，願君伐之，請出兵以為外援。

translations.literal: Shangliao is very rich and substantial—I hope you will attack it; please send troops as external aid."
translations.idiomatic: Shangliao is rich and well stocked. I beg you to attack it, and I will send troops as your ally."

sentences.zh: 」且以珠寶、葛越賂勳。

translations.literal: " He also bribed Xun with jewels and Ge Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent jewels and the warrior Ge Yue as gifts.

sentences.zh: 勳大喜，外內盡賀，劉曄獨否，勳問其故，對曰：「上繚雖小，城堅池深，攻難守易，不可旬日而舉也。

translations.literal: Xun was greatly delighted; inside and outside all congratulated him—only Liu Ye dissented. Xun asked the reason, and he replied, "Though Shangliao is small, its walls are strong and moats deep—hard to attack, easy to defend; it cannot be taken in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was overjoyed, and everyone congratulated him—only Liu Ye objected. When Xun asked why, Ye replied, "Shangliao is small but its walls are strong and its moats deep. It is hard to attack and easy to defend, and cannot be taken in ten days.

sentences.zh: 兵疲於外而國內虛，策乘虛襲我，則後不能獨守。

translations.literal: Troops exhausted outside while the state within is empty—Ce will seize the emptiness to strike us, and afterward we cannot defend alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your troops will be exhausted abroad while your base is empty. Ce will seize the opening and strike, and you will not be able to hold your ground alone.

sentences.zh: 是將軍進屈於敵，退無所歸，若軍必出，禍今至矣。

translations.literal: Then the general advances and is bent by the enemy, retreats with nowhere to return—if the army must go out, disaster arrives now.
translations.idiomatic: You will be humbled before the enemy in the field and have nowhere to retreat. If you march out, disaster is upon you now."

sentences.zh: 」勳不聽，遂伐上繚；

translations.literal: " Xun did not listen and therefore attacked Shangliao;
translations.idiomatic: Xun would not listen and marched against Shangliao.

sentences.zh: 至海昏，宗帥知之，皆空壁逃遷，勳了無所得。

translations.literal: when he reached Haihun the clan chieftains learned of it and all emptied their walls and fled—Xun obtained nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: At Haihun the clan chieftains learned of his approach, abandoned their strongholds, and fled. Xun gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 時策引兵西擊黃祖，行及石城，聞勳在海昏，策乃分遣從兄賁、輔將八千人屯彭澤，自與領江夏太守周瑜將二萬人襲皖城，克之，得術、勳妻子及部曲三萬餘人；

translations.literal: At that time Ce was leading troops west to attack Huang Zu; marching as far as Shicheng, he heard Xun was at Haihun. Ce then separately sent his cousins Ben and Fu with eight thousand to garrison at Pengze, while he himself with the Acting Jiangxia Administrator Zhou Yu led twenty thousand to strike Wancheng, captured it, and obtained Shu's and Xun's wives and children and more than thirty thousand followers;
translations.idiomatic: Ce was marching west against Huang Zu and had reached Shicheng when he learned Xun was at Haihun. He detached his cousins Sun Ben and Sun Fu with eight thousand men to hold Pengze, while he and the acting Jiangxia administrator Zhou Yu led twenty thousand in a surprise attack on Wancheng. The city fell, and he seized the families of Shu and Xun along with more than thirty thousand followers;

sentences.zh: 表汝南李術為廬江太守，給兵三千人以守皖城，皆徙所得民東詣吳。

translations.literal: he appointed Li Shu of Runan as Lujiang Administrator, gave three thousand troops to guard Wancheng, and moved all the people obtained east to Wu territory.
translations.idiomatic: appointed Li Shu of Runan Lujiang administrator, left three thousand troops to hold Wancheng, and resettled the captives eastward in Wu territory.

sentences.zh: 勳還至彭澤，孫賁、孫輔邀擊，破之。

translations.literal: Xun returned to Pengze; Sun Ben and Sun Fu intercepted and struck him and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun retreated to Pengze, where Sun Ben and Sun Fu intercepted and routed him.

sentences.zh: 勳走保流沂，求救於黃祖，祖遣其子射率船軍五千人助勳。

translations.literal: Xun fled to defend Liuyi and begged rescue from Huang Zu; Zu sent his son She leading five thousand men in a fleet to aid Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled to Liuyi and begged Huang Zu for aid. Zu sent his son She with a fleet of five thousand to help him.

sentences.zh: 策復就攻勳，大破之，勳北歸曹操，射亦遁走。

translations.literal: Ce again pressed to attack Xun, utterly defeated him; Xun fled north to submit to Cao Cao, and She also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ce pressed the attack, routed Xun utterly, and Xun fled north to Cao Cao while She also escaped.

sentences.zh: 策收得勳兵二千餘人，船千艘，遂進擊黃祖。

translations.literal: Ce collected more than two thousand of Xun's troops and a thousand boats, then advanced to attack Huang Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Ce took more than two thousand of Xun's troops and a thousand boats, then marched on Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛亥，策軍至沙羨，劉表遣從子虎及南陽韓晞，將長矛五千來救祖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinhai day, Ce's army reached Shaxian; Liu Biao sent his cousin Hu and Han Xi of Nanyang leading five thousand long-spearmen to rescue Zu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day xinhai, Ce's army reached Shaxian. Liu Biao sent his cousin Hu and Han Xi of Nanyang with five thousand pikemen to rescue Zu.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，策與戰，大破之，斬晞。

translations.literal: On jiayin day Ce fought them, utterly defeated them, and beheaded Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin Ce engaged them, won a crushing victory, and beheaded Xi.

sentences.zh: 祖脫身走，獲其妻子及船六千艘，士卒殺溺死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Zu escaped with his body; Ce captured his wife and children and six thousand boats; soldiers killed and drowned numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zu himself escaped, but Ce captured his family and six thousand boats. Tens of thousands of his men were killed or drowned.

sentences.zh: 策盛兵將徇豫章，屯於椒丘，謂功曹虞翻曰：「華子魚自有名字，然非吾敵也。

translations.literal: Ce massed troops and was about to overrun Yuzhang, encamping at Jiaoqiu. He said to the Merit Officer Yu Fan, "Hua Ziyu has his own reputation, yet he is not my match."
translations.idiomatic: Ce gathered his forces to overrun Yuzhang and encamped at Jiaoqiu. He told the merit officer Yu Fan, "Hua Ziyu has a name, but he is no match for me."

sentences.zh: 若不開門讓城，金鼓一震，不得無所傷害。

translations.literal: If he does not open the gates and yield the city, when drums and bells shake once, there cannot fail to be harm.
translations.idiomatic: If he does not open the gates and yield the city, when the drums sound there will surely be bloodshed."

sentences.zh: 卿便在前，具宣孤意。

translations.literal: You go ahead and fully proclaim my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Go before me and make my intentions plain."

sentences.zh: 」翻乃往見華歆曰：「竊聞明府與鄙郡故王府君齊名中州，海內所宗，雖在東垂，常懷瞻仰。

translations.literal: " Fan then went to see Hua Xin and said, "I have heard that my lord and the former Wang lord of our humble commandery were equally famed in the central provinces, honored throughout the realm—though in the eastern reaches, I have long looked up in admiration."
translations.idiomatic: Fan went to see Hua Xin and said, "I have heard that you and the former Wang lord of our region were equally renowned in the central provinces and honored throughout the realm. Though we are in the eastern marches, we have long looked to you with admiration."

sentences.zh: 」歆曰：「孤不如王會稽。

translations.literal: " Xin said, "I am not the equal of Wang of Kuaiji."
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "I am not the equal of Wang of Kuaiji."

sentences.zh: 」翻復曰：「不早豫章資糧器仗，士民勇果，孰與鄙郡？

translations.literal: " Fan again said, "Were Yuzhang's provisions, weapons, and gear, and the courage of its people and soldiers, prepared early—how would they compare with our humble commandery?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan pressed on: "Were Yuzhang's stores, arms, and the courage of its people prepared in advance, how would they compare with our region?"

sentences.zh: 」歆曰：「大不如也。

translations.literal: " Xin said, "Far inferior."
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "Far inferior."

sentences.zh: 」翻曰：「明府言不如王會稽，謙光之譚耳；

translations.literal: " Fan said, "My lord's saying you are not the equal of Wang of Kuaiji is merely modest talk;
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "When you say you are not Wang's equal, that is mere modesty;

sentences.zh: 精兵不如會稽，實如尊教。

translations.literal: that elite troops are not the equal of Kuaiji's is truly as my lord teaches.
translations.idiomatic: but that your elite troops are inferior to Kuaiji's is, as you yourself admit, the truth.

sentences.zh: 孫討逆智略超世，用兵如神，前走劉揚州，君所親見；

translations.literal: Lord Sun the Campaigner Against Rebels has strategy surpassing the age and uses troops like a spirit—before he routed Liu of Yang Province, which my lord saw with his own eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Sun the Campaigner Against Rebels surpasses his age in strategy and wields his army like a spirit. You saw with your own eyes how he routed Liu of Yang Province;

sentences.zh: 南定鄙郡，亦君所聞也。

translations.literal: southward he settled our humble commandery, which my lord has also heard.
translations.idiomatic: and you have heard how he pacified our region to the south.

sentences.zh: 今欲守孤城，自料資糧，已知不足，不早為計，悔無及也。

translations.literal: Now wishing to hold an isolated city, estimating provisions yourself, you already know they are insufficient—if you do not plan early, regret will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to hold this isolated city, you know your stores are insufficient. If you do not act now, it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 今大軍已次椒丘，僕便還去，明日日中迎檄不到者，與君辭矣。

translations.literal: Now the great army has already halted at Jiaoqiu—I return at once; tomorrow at noon, whoever does not come to receive the proclamation, I take leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: The main army is already at Jiaoqiu. I return now. Tomorrow at noon, whoever has not come to receive the surrender order, I bid you farewell."

sentences.zh: 」歆曰：「久在江表，常欲北歸；

translations.literal: " Xin said, "Long in the lands south of the Yangzi, I have often wished to return north;
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "I have long dwelt south of the Yangzi and often wished to return north.

sentences.zh: 孫會稽來，吾便去也。

translations.literal: when Lord Sun of Kuaiji comes, I shall go."
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Sun of Kuaiji comes, I shall go."

sentences.zh: 」乃夜作檄，明旦，遣吏繼迎。

translations.literal: " He then drafted a surrender proclamation that night, and at dawn sent officials in succession to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: That night he drafted a surrender proclamation, and at dawn sent officials out in succession to welcome Ce's army.

sentences.zh: 策便進軍，歆葛巾迎策，策謂歆曰：「府君年德名望，遠近所歸；

translations.literal: Ce immediately advanced his army; Xin in hemp headcloth welcomed Ce. Ce said to Xin, "My lord's years, virtue, and reputation are what near and far return to;
translations.idiomatic: Ce advanced at once. Xin came out in plain hemp cloth to welcome him. Ce said, "Your years, virtue, and reputation draw men from far and near;

sentences.zh: 策年幼稚，宜修子弟之禮。

translations.literal: Ce is young and immature—I ought to observe the rites of a junior to an elder."
translations.idiomatic: I am young and ought to observe the rites due a junior kinsman."

sentences.zh: 」便向歆拜，禮為上賓。

translations.literal: " He then bowed to Xin and treated him with the rites due a supreme guest.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to Xin and treated him as a guest of the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：歆既無夷、皓韜邈之風，又失王臣匪躬之操，橈心於邪儒之說，交臂於陵肆之徒，位奪節墮，咎孰大焉！

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: Xin had neither the reclusive wind of Boyi and Shuqi nor the unswerving integrity of a royal minister who does not spare himself; he bent his heart to the doctrines of perverse scholars and locked arms with insolent ruffians—office seized, integrity fallen—what fault could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng wrote: Xin possessed neither the reclusive integrity of Boyi and Shuqi nor the unswerving loyalty of a minister who sacrifices himself for his lord. He bent his heart to perverse doctrine and clasped arms with insolent men—office seized, honor fallen. What fault could be greater?

sentences.zh: 策分豫章為廬陵郡，以孫賁為豫章太守，孫輔為廬陵太守。

translations.literal: Ce divided Yuzhang to form Luling commandery, appointing Sun Ben as Yuzhang Administrator and Sun Fu as Luling Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Ce carved Luling commandery out of Yuzhang, appointing Sun Ben Yuzhang administrator and Sun Fu Luling administrator.

sentences.zh: 會僮芝病，輔遂進屯廬陵，留周瑜鎮巴丘。

translations.literal: When Tong Zhi fell ill, Fu advanced to garrison at Luling and left Zhou Yu to guard Baqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Zhi fell ill, Fu advanced to garrison Luling while Zhou Yu was left to hold Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 孫策之克皖城也，撫視袁術妻子；

translations.literal: When Sun Ce captured Wancheng, he comforted and looked after Yuan Shu's wife and children;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce took Wancheng, he treated Yuan Shu's family with care;

sentences.zh: 及入豫章，收載劉繇喪，善遇其家。

translations.literal: when he entered Yuzhang he collected and conveyed Liu Yao's funeral and treated his family well.
translations.idiomatic: and on entering Yuzhang he saw that Liu Yao received proper burial and treated Liu's family kindly.

sentences.zh: 士大夫以是稱之。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 會稽功曹魏騰嘗策意，策將殺之，眾憂恐，計無所出。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji Merit Officer Wei Teng had once opposed Ce's intentions; Ce was about to kill him, and the crowd was worried and afraid with no plan to offer.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji merit officer Wei Teng had once opposed Ce's plans, and Ce was about to execute him. His officers were terrified and could think of no remedy.

sentences.zh: 策母吳夫人倚大井謂策曰：「汝新造江南，其事未集，方當優賢禮士，捨過錄功。

translations.literal: Ce's mother, Lady Wu, leaned on the great well and said to Ce, "You have newly built the south of the Yangzi; affairs are not yet gathered. You should just now honor the worthy and treat scholars with rites, pardon faults and record merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's mother, Lady Wu, leaned on the great well and said to him, "You have only lately built your power in the south, and your enterprise is not yet secure. You should honor the worthy, treat scholars with courtesy, pardon faults, and reward merit.

sentences.zh: 魏功曹在公盡規，汝今日殺之，則明日人皆叛汝。

translations.literal: The Wei Merit Officer remonstrated to the utmost before the lord—if you kill him today, then tomorrow all men will rebel against you.
translations.idiomatic: Wei remonstrated with you to the utmost. If you kill him today, tomorrow every man will turn against you.

sentences.zh: 吾不忍見禍之及，當先投此井中耳！

translations.literal: I cannot bear to see disaster reach you—I will first cast myself into this well!"
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to see disaster overtake you—I will cast myself into this well first!"

sentences.zh: 」策大驚，遽釋騰。

translations.literal: " Ce was greatly startled and immediately released Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was greatly startled and at once released Teng.

sentences.zh: 初，吳郡太守會稽盛憲舉高岱孝廉。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wu Commandery Administrator Sheng Xian of Kuaiji had nominated Gao Dai as a filial and incorrupt candidate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Wu commandery administrator Sheng Xian of Kuaiji had nominated Gao Dai as a filial and incorrupt candidate.

sentences.zh: 許貢來領郡，岱將憲避難於營帥許昭家。

translations.literal: Xu Gong came to take charge of the commandery; Dai led Xian to take refuge at the camp commander Xu Zhao's home.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Gong came to take the commandery, Dai led Xian to refuge at the camp commander Xu Zhao's home.

sentences.zh: 烏程鄒佗、錢銅及嘉興王晟等各聚眾萬餘或數千人，不附孫策。

translations.literal: Zou Tuo and Qian Tong of Wucheng and Wang Sheng of Jiaxing and others each gathered followers of ten thousand or several thousand and did not attach themselves to Sun Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Tuo and Qian Tong of Wucheng, Wang Sheng of Jiaxing, and others each raised bands of ten thousand or several thousand men and refused to submit to Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 策引兵撲討，皆破之，進攻嚴白虎。

translations.literal: Ce led troops to strike and suppress them, defeating them all, and advanced to attack Yan Baihu.
translations.idiomatic: Ce led troops against them, defeated them all, and advanced to attack Yan Baihu.

sentences.zh: 白虎兵敗，奔餘杭，投許昭。

translations.literal: Baihu's troops were defeated; he fled to Yuhang and threw himself on Xu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Baihu was defeated and fled to Yuhang, seeking refuge with Xu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 程普請擊昭，策曰：「許昭有義於舊君，有誠於故友，此丈夫之志也。

translations.literal: Cheng Pu requested to attack Zhao; Ce said, "Xu Zhao showed righteousness toward his former lord and sincerity toward an old friend—this is the resolve of a true man."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pu asked permission to attack Zhao. Ce said, "Xu Zhao showed loyalty to his former lord and faithfulness to an old friend. That is the conduct of a true man."

sentences.zh: 」乃捨之。

translations.literal: " He therefore released him.
translations.idiomatic: He spared him.

sentences.zh: 曹操復屯官渡。

translations.literal: Cao Cao again encamped at Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao again took up camp at Guandu.

sentences.zh: 操常從士徐他等謀殺操，入操帳，見校尉許褚，色變，褚覺而殺之。

translations.literal: Among Cao's personal attendants, Xu Ta and others plotted to kill Cao; they entered Cao's tent, saw the Commandant Xu Chu, changed color, and Chu perceived it and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Among Cao Cao's personal attendants, Xu Ta and others plotted to assassinate him. They entered Cao's tent, saw the commandant Xu Chu, and their faces changed. Chu noticed and killed them.

sentences.zh: 初，車騎將軍董承稱受帝衣帶中密詔，與劉備謀誅曹操。

translations.literal: Earlier, the General of Chariots and Cavalry Dong Cheng claimed to have received a secret edict hidden in the Emperor's girdle, and conspired with Liu Bei to execute Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the general of chariots and cavalry Dong Cheng claimed he had received a secret edict concealed in the emperor's girdle and plotted with Liu Bei to kill Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操從容謂備曰：「今天下英雄，惟使君與操耳，本初之徒，不足數也！

translations.literal: Cao said calmly to Bei, "Of all the heroes under heaven today, only Your Lordship and I count; the likes of Benchu are not worth numbering!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said calmly to Liu Bei, "Of all the heroes under heaven today, only you and I count. Benchu's sort are not worth mentioning!

sentences.zh: 」備方食，失匕箸，值天雷震，備因曰：「聖人云：『迅雷風烈必變』，良有以也。

translations.literal: " Bei was just eating and dropped his spoon and chopsticks; thunder pealed from the sky, and Bei therefore said, "The sage said, 'When thunder roars and wind howls, one must change'—there is truly reason in it.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei was midway through his meal and dropped his spoon and chopsticks. Thunder crashed overhead, and Liu Bei seized the moment to say, "The sage said, 'When thunder rolls and the gale rises, one must change'—and he was right.

sentences.zh: 」遂與承及長水校尉種輯、將軍吳子蘭、王服等同謀。

translations.literal: " He then plotted together with Cheng, the Changshui Commandant Zhong Ji, the generals Wu Zilan and Wang Fu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Dong Cheng, the Changshui commandant Zhong Ji, the generals Wu Zilan and Wang Fu, and others in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 會操遣備與朱靈邀袁術，程昱、郭嘉、董昭皆諫曰：「備不可遣也！

translations.literal: When Cao sent Bei with Zhu Ling to intercept Yuan Shu, Cheng Yu, Guo Jia, and Dong Zhao all remonstrated, saying, "Bei must not be sent away!
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao dispatched Liu Bei with Zhu Ling to intercept Yuan Shu, Cheng Yu, Guo Jia, and Dong Zhao all remonstrated: "Liu Bei must not be sent away!

sentences.zh: 」操悔，追之，不及。

translations.literal: " Cao regretted it and pursued him but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao regretted it and gave chase but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 術既南走，朱靈等還。

translations.literal: After Shu had fled south, Zhu Ling and the others returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shu fled south, Zhu Ling and the others returned.

sentences.zh: 備遂殺徐州刺史車冑，留關羽守下邳，行太守事，身還小沛。

translations.literal: Bei then killed the Xu Province Inspector Che Zhou, left Guan Yu to hold Xiapi and act as Administrator, and himself returned to Xiaopei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei then killed the Xu province inspector Che Zhou, left Guan Yu to hold Xiapi and serve as acting administrator, and returned in person to Xiaopei.

sentences.zh: 東海賊昌豨及郡縣多叛操為備。

translations.literal: The bandit Chang Xi of Donghai and many commanderies and counties rebelled against Cao to join Bei.
translations.idiomatic: The Donghai bandit Chang Xi and many counties rebelled against Cao Cao to side with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備眾數萬人，遣使與袁紹連兵。

translations.literal: Bei's followers numbered tens of thousands; he sent envoys to join forces with Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei mustered tens of thousands of followers and sent envoys to join Yuan Shao in alliance.

sentences.zh: 操遣司空長史沛國劉岱、中郎將扶風王忠擊之，不克。

translations.literal: Cao sent the Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Liu Dai of Pei and the General of the Household Wang Zhong of Fufeng to attack him, but they could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent the chief clerk of the minister of works Liu Dai of Pei and the general of the household Wang Zhong of Fufeng against him, but they failed to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 備謂岱等曰：「使汝百人來，無如我何；

translations.literal: Bei said to Dai and the others, "Send a hundred men like you—I care nothing for you;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei said to Dai and the others, "Send a hundred men like you, and you will still be no match for me;

sentences.zh: 曹公自來，未可知耳！

translations.literal: if Lord Cao comes himself, that cannot yet be known!
translations.idiomatic: but if Lord Cao comes in person—that is another matter entirely!

translations.literal: [closing quote]
translations.idiomatic: [closing quote]

sentences.zh: 春，正月，董承謀洩；

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Dong Cheng's plot was leaked;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Dong Cheng's plot was exposed;

sentences.zh: 壬子，曹操殺承及王服、種輯，皆夷三族。

translations.literal: On renzi Cao Cao executed Cheng and Wang Fu and Zhong Ji, all exterminating three clans.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi, Cao Cao executed Dong Cheng, Wang Fu, and Zhong Ji, exterminating all three clans in each case.

sentences.zh: 操欲自討劉備，諸將皆曰：「與公爭天下者，袁紹也，今紹方來而棄之東，紹乘人後，若何？

translations.literal: Cao wished to march personally against Liu Bei; all the generals said, "He who contends with you for the realm is Yuan Shao; now Shao is just coming—if you abandon him and go east, Shao will take advantage from behind—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wished to march east against Liu Bei in person. His generals all said, "He who contests the realm with you is Yuan Shao. Shao is advancing even now—if you turn east and leave him behind, he will seize the opportunity from the rear. What then?

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「劉備，人傑也，今不擊，必為後患。

translations.literal: " Cao said, "Liu Bei is a transcendent man; if he is not struck down now, he will surely become a trouble hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Liu Bei is a transcendent man. If we do not strike him down now, he will surely become a trouble hereafter.

sentences.zh: 」郭嘉曰：「紹性遲而多疑，來必不速。

translations.literal: " Guo Jia said, "Shao's nature is slow and he is much given to suspicion; when he comes, he will surely not be swift.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia said, "Yuan Shao is slow by nature and much given to suspicion. When he moves, he will not be swift.

sentences.zh: 備新起，眾心未附，急擊之，必敗。

translations.literal: Bei has newly risen and the hearts of the masses are not yet attached; strike him urgently and he will surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei has only just risen, and his followers' loyalty is not yet firm. Strike quickly and he will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 」操師遂東。

translations.literal: " Cao's army thereupon marched east.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's army marched east.

sentences.zh: 冀州別駕田豐說袁紹曰：「曹操與劉備連兵，未可卒解。

translations.literal: Tian Feng, Administrator of Ji Province, advised Yuan Shao, saying, "Cao Cao is joined in arms with Liu Bei and cannot quickly be released.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Feng, the Ji province administrator, urged Yuan Shao, "Cao Cao and Liu Bei are allied in arms. The crisis will not end quickly.

sentences.zh: 公舉軍而襲其後，可一往而定。

translations.literal: My lord should raise the whole army and strike him from behind—one march and it can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Raise your whole army and strike him from the rear. One campaign and the matter will be settled.

sentences.zh: 」紹辭以子疾，未得行。

translations.literal: " Shao declined on the grounds that his son was ill and could not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao declined, pleading his son's illness, and did not march.

sentences.zh: 豐舉杖擊地曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: Feng raised his staff and struck the ground, saying, "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Feng lifted his staff and struck the ground. "Alas!" he cried.

sentences.zh: 遭難遇之時，而以嬰兒病失其會，惜哉，事去矣！

translations.literal: To meet a time of hardship and yet lose the opportunity because of an infant's illness—how regrettable! The affair has passed!
translations.idiomatic: In a crisis such as this, to lose the moment over a child's sickness! What a pity—the opportunity is gone!

sentences.zh: 」曹操擊劉備，破之，獲其妻子；

translations.literal: " Cao Cao attacked Liu Bei, defeated him, and captured his wife and children;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao attacked Liu Bei, routed him, and captured his wife and children;

sentences.zh: 進拔下邳，禽關羽；

translations.literal: advanced and took Xiapi, capturing Guan Yu;
translations.idiomatic: advanced to Xiapi and captured Guan Yu;

sentences.zh: 又擊昌豨，破之。

translations.literal: he also attacked Chang Xi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: and also defeated Chang Xi.

sentences.zh: 備奔青州，因袁譚以歸袁紹。

translations.literal: Bei fled to Qing Province and, through Yuan Tan, returned to Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei fled to Qing province and, through Yuan Tan, rejoined Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹聞備至，去鄴二百里迎之，駐月餘，所亡士卒稍稍歸之。

translations.literal: When Shao heard Bei had arrived, he went two hundred li from Ye to welcome him, and halted for more than a month; soldiers who had scattered gradually returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao heard Liu Bei had arrived, he went two hundred li from Ye to welcome him and kept him for more than a month. Liu Bei's scattered troops gradually returned.

sentences.zh: 曹操還軍官渡，紹乃議攻許，田豐曰：「曹操既破劉備，則許下非復空虛。

translations.literal: Cao Cao returned his army to Guandu; Shao then deliberated attacking Xu; Tian Feng said, "Cao Cao having already defeated Liu Bei, Xu below is no longer empty as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao returned to Guandu. Yuan Shao then debated attacking Xu. Tian Feng said, "Cao Cao has already defeated Liu Bei. Xu is no longer undefended.

sentences.zh: 且操善用兵，變化無方，眾雖少，未可輕也，今不如以久持之。

translations.literal: Moreover Cao is skilled at using troops and transforms without fixed pattern; though his forces are few, he cannot be treated lightly—now it is better to hold to a long contest.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Cao Cao is skilled in war and changes his tactics without pattern. Though his forces are few, they must not be taken lightly. Better to wear him down over time.

sentences.zh: 將軍據山河之固，擁四州之眾，外結英雄，內修農戰，然後簡其精銳，分為奇兵，乘虛迭出以擾河南，救右則擊其左，救左則擊其右，使敵疲於奔命，民不得安業，我未勞而彼已困，不及三年，可坐克也。

translations.literal: The general holds the firmness of mountains and rivers and commands the multitudes of four provinces; abroad ally with heroes, at home cultivate farming and warfare—then select the elite and sharp, divide them into strike forces, ride emptiness in successive raids to harass Henan, save the right and strike the left, save the left and strike the right, making the enemy weary from running to save each side and the people unable to settle to their livelihood—we not yet weary while they already exhausted, and in less than three years can conquer while seated.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the natural defenses of the Yellow River and Taihang, command the people of four provinces, win allies abroad, and train farmers for war at home. Then pick your best troops, divide them into mobile columns, and raid Henan again and again wherever the enemy is weak. When they reinforce one flank, strike the other; when they save the left, hit the right. Wear the enemy out in constant marches and rob the people of any peace. We need not exhaust ourselves while they collapse—in less than three years you can win without leaving your seat.

sentences.zh: 今釋廟勝之策而決成敗於一戰，若不如志，悔無及也。

translations.literal: Now you abandon the strategy that wins in the temple and decide victory and defeat in a single battle—if it does not go as you wish, regret will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Now you cast aside careful planning to stake everything on one battle. If it fails, there will be no undoing it.

sentences.zh: 」紹不從。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 豐強諫忤紹，紹以為沮眾，械系之。

translations.literal: Feng remonstrated strongly and offended Shao; Shao regarded him as dispiriting the army and had him fettered and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Feng pressed his advice until Yuan Shao took offense. Shao judged him a demoralizer and had him put in chains.

sentences.zh: 於是移檄州郡，數操罪惡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued a proclamation to the provinces and commanderies, enumerating Cao's crimes and wickedness.
