translations.idiomatic: He then sent a proclamation through the provinces, listing Cao Cao's crimes.

sentences.zh: 二月，進軍黎陽。

translations.literal: In the second month he advanced his army to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he marched to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 沮授臨行，會其宗族，散資財以與之曰：「勢存則威無不加，勢亡則不保一身，哀哉！

translations.literal: Ju Shou, on the eve of departure, gathered his clan and distributed his wealth and property to them, saying, "While power stands, majesty is added without limit; when power perishes one cannot preserve even one's own person—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Before setting out, Ju Shou gathered his clan and divided his estate among them. "While fortune holds," he said, "power knows no limit. When fortune fails, a man cannot even save himself. How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 」其弟宗曰：「曹操士馬不敵，君何懼焉？

translations.literal: " His younger brother Zong said, "Cao Cao's men and horses cannot match ours—why do you fear?
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ju Zong said, "Cao Cao's men and horses are no match for ours. Why so much fear?

sentences.zh: 」授曰：「以曹操之明略，又挾天子以為資，我雖克伯珪，眾實疲敝，而主驕將忲，軍之破敗，在此舉矣。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "With Cao Cao's brilliance and strategy, and moreover holding the Son of Heaven as his resource—though we conquered Boqi, our forces are in truth wearied and depleted, and the lord is arrogant and the generals reckless—the army's defeat lies in this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou said, "Cao Cao is brilliant in counsel and holds the Son of Heaven as his weapon. Though we conquered Gongsun Zan, our army is exhausted. Our lord grows proud and our generals reckless. Defeat waits in this campaign.

sentences.zh: 揚雄有言：『六國蚩蚩，為嬴弱姬。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong said, 'The six states in turmoil served as the weakened wives of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong wrote: 'The six states in chaos became Qin's tame concubines.

sentences.zh: 』其今之謂乎！

translations.literal: ' Does this not describe the present!
translations.idiomatic: ' Is that not exactly our case today?

translations.literal: [closing quote]
translations.idiomatic: [closing quote]

sentences.zh: 振威將軍程昱以七百兵守鄄城。

translations.literal: The General Who Displays Martial Power Cheng Yu held Juancheng with seven hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu, general who displays martial power, held Juancheng with seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 曹操欲益昱兵二千，昱不肯，曰：「袁紹擁十萬眾，自以所向無前，今見昱少兵，必輕易，不來攻。

translations.literal: Cao Cao wished to increase Yu's troops by two thousand; Yu refused, saying, "Yuan Shao commands a hundred thousand followers and considers himself unmatched wherever he goes; now seeing Yu's few troops he will surely treat it lightly and not come to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wanted to reinforce him with two thousand more men. Cheng Yu refused. "Yuan Shao commands a hundred thousand men and deems himself invincible," he said. "Seeing my few troops, he will surely despise the target and leave us alone.

sentences.zh: 若益昱兵，過則不可不攻，攻之必克，徒兩損其勢，願公無疑。

translations.literal: If Yu's troops are increased, when he passes he cannot fail to attack; if he attacks he will surely be taken—worthlessly damaging strength on both sides; I hope my lord will have no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: If you strengthen my garrison, he cannot pass without attacking; and if he attacks, he must take the city—wasting strength on both sides for nothing. Have no fear, my lord.

sentences.zh: 」紹聞昱兵少，果不往，操謂賈詡曰：「程昱之膽，過於賁、育矣！

translations.literal: " When Shao heard Yu's troops were few, he indeed did not go; Cao said to Jia Xu, "Cheng Yu's courage surpasses Meng Ben and Xia Yu!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao heard how few Cheng Yu's men were and, as predicted, did not attack. Cao Cao told Jia Xu, "Cheng Yu's courage surpasses that of Meng Ben and Xia Yu!

translations.literal: [closing quote]
translations.idiomatic: [closing quote]

sentences.zh: 袁紹遣其將顏良攻東郡太守劉延於白馬，沮授曰：「良性促狹，雖驍勇，不可獨任。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao sent his general Yan Liang to attack the Administrator of Dong Commandery Liu Yan at Baima; Ju Shou said, "Liang's nature is narrow and impatient; though fierce and brave, he cannot be entrusted alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent his general Yan Liang to attack Liu Yan, administrator of Dong commandery, at Baima. Ju Shou warned, "Yan Liang is impulsive and narrow-minded. Brave as he is, he should not be given independent command.

sentences.zh: 」紹不聽。

translations.literal: " Shao did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，曹操北救劉延。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao went north to rescue Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Cao Cao marched north to relieve Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 荀攸曰：「今兵少不敵，必分其勢乃可。

translations.literal: Xun You said, "Now our troops are few and cannot match—his force must be divided before it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said, "We are too few to meet him head-on. We must split his strength first.

sentences.zh: 公到延津，若將渡兵向其後者，紹必西應之，然後輕兵襲白馬，掩其不備，顏良可禽也。

translations.literal: When my lord reaches Yanjin, if you make as if to cross the river toward his rear, Shao will surely respond westward; then with light troops strike Baima, catching him unprepared—Yan Liang can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: March to Yanjin and feign crossing the river against his rear. Shao will wheel west to meet you. Then strike Baima with a light column before he is ready, and Yan Liang can be taken.

sentences.zh: 」操從之，紹聞兵渡，即分兵西邀之。

translations.literal: " Cao followed this; when Shao heard troops were crossing, he immediately divided troops to intercept them westward.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed. When Shao heard the river crossing, he split his forces to block them in the west.

sentences.zh: 操乃引軍兼行趣白馬，未至十餘里，良大驚，來逆戰。

translations.literal: Cao then led his army by forced marches toward Baima; before they were ten-odd li away, Liang was greatly alarmed and came to meet in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then drove his army at speed toward Baima. Less than ten li away, Yan Liang was alarmed and rode out to give battle.

sentences.zh: 操使張遼、關羽先登擊之。

translations.literal: Cao sent Zhang Liao and Guan Yu to lead the van in striking him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Zhang Liao and Guan Yu at the head of the assault.

sentences.zh: 羽望見良麾蓋，策馬刺良於萬眾之中，斬其首而還，紹軍莫能當者。

translations.literal: Yu saw Liang's command banner, spurred his horse and stabbed Liang among ten thousand men, cut off his head and returned; none in Shao's army could stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu spotted Yan Liang's command banner, spurred his horse through ten thousand men, ran him through, and returned with his head. No one in Shao's army could stop him.

sentences.zh: 遂解白馬之圍，徙其民，循河而西。

translations.literal: The siege of Baima was thereby lifted; he moved its people and went west along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Baima was lifted. Cao Cao evacuated the populace and withdrew west along the river.

sentences.zh: 紹渡河追之，沮授諫曰：「勝負變化，不可不詳。

translations.literal: Shao crossed the river in pursuit; Ju Shou remonstrated, saying, "Victory and defeat shift—this cannot but be examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao crossed the river in pursuit. Ju Shou remonstrated, "Fortunes of war are changeable. This must be weighed carefully.

sentences.zh: 今宜留屯延津；

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to remain encamped at Yanjin;
translations.idiomatic: Hold Yanjin with a strong camp;

sentences.zh: 分兵官渡，若其克獲，還迎不晚，設其有難，眾弗可還。

translations.literal: send divided troops to Guandu; if they capture victory there, turning back to welcome is not late; if there is difficulty, the masses cannot return.
translations.idiomatic: and detach troops toward Guandu. If they succeed, it is not too late to welcome them back. If disaster strikes, the whole army may not return.

sentences.zh: 」紹弗從。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao refused.

sentences.zh: 授臨濟歎曰：「上盈其志，下務其功，悠悠黃河，吾其濟乎！

translations.literal: Shou, on reaching the ford, sighed and said, "Above, his ambition overflows; below, they strive for merit—vast Yellow River, shall I cross it!
translations.idiomatic: At the ford Ju Shou sighed, "Our lord's ambition runs too high, and his officers chase glory. Vast Yellow River—shall I ever cross back?

sentences.zh: 」遂以疾辭。

translations.literal: " He therefore pleaded illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 紹不許而意恨之，復省其所部並屬郭圖。

translations.literal: Shao did not permit it but harbored resentment toward him, and again reduced what he commanded, merging it under Guo Tu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao refused but nursed resentment, stripped him of command, and merged his troops under Guo Tu.

sentences.zh: 紹軍至延津南，操勒兵駐營南阪下，使登壘望之，曰：「可五六百騎。

translations.literal: Shao's army reached south of Yanjin; Cao led troops and encamped on the southern slope, sent men up the ramparts to look, and said, "Perhaps five or six hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's army reached the south bank of Yanjin. Cao Cao drew up on the southern slope and sent scouts onto the ramparts. "Five or six hundred horsemen, no more," he said.

sentences.zh: 」有頃，復白：「騎稍多，步兵不可勝數。

translations.literal: " After a little while they reported again, "Horsemen somewhat more—infantry cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later they reported again: "More horsemen—infantry beyond count.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「勿復白。

translations.literal: " Cao said, "Do not report again.
translations.idiomatic: "Say no more," Cao Cao ordered.

sentences.zh: 」令騎解鞍放馬。

translations.literal: " He ordered the horsemen to un saddle and loose the horses.
translations.idiomatic: He had the horsemen unsaddle and turn their mounts loose.

sentences.zh: 是時，白馬輜重就道，諸將以為敵騎多，不如還保營。

translations.literal: At this time Baima's baggage train was on the road; the generals thought the enemy horsemen many and that it would be better to return and protect the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Baima's supply train was still on the road. His generals, seeing the enemy cavalry massing, wanted to fall back and protect the camp.

sentences.zh: 荀攸曰：「此所以餌敵，如何去之！

translations.literal: Xun You said, "This is precisely to bait the enemy—how can you abandon it!
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said, "This is bait for the enemy. How can we abandon it?

sentences.zh: 」操顧攸而笑。

translations.literal: " Cao looked at You and smiled.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao glanced at Xun You and smiled.

sentences.zh: 紹騎將文丑與劉備將五六千騎前後至。

translations.literal: Shao's cavalry general Wen Chou, with Liu Bei's five or six thousand horsemen, arrived before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's cavalry general Wen Chou arrived with Liu Bei's five or six thousand horsemen, one column after another.

sentences.zh: 諸將復白：「可上馬。

translations.literal: The generals reported again, "One can mount.
translations.idiomatic: His officers reported again, "We should mount.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「未也。

translations.literal: " Cao said, "Not yet.
translations.idiomatic: "Not yet," Cao Cao said.

sentences.zh: 」有頃，騎至稍多，或分趣輜重。

translations.literal: " After a little while horsemen arrived somewhat more, some diverging toward the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: A little later more horsemen arrived, some peeling off toward the supply train.

sentences.zh: 操曰：「可矣！

translations.literal: Cao said, "Now!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao cried, "Now!"

sentences.zh: 」乃皆上馬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Every man mounted.

sentences.zh: 時騎不滿六百，遂縱兵擊，大破之，斬丑。

translations.literal: At that time the horsemen numbered fewer than six hundred; he then loosed his troops to attack, utterly defeated them, and beheaded Chou.
translations.idiomatic: They had fewer than six hundred horsemen. Cao Cao charged, broke the enemy, and beheaded Wen Chou.

sentences.zh: 丑與顏良，皆紹名將也，再戰，悉禽之，紹軍奪氣。

translations.literal: Chou and Yan Liang were both famed generals of Shao; in two battles all were captured—in Shao's army spirits were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Chou and Yan Liang were Shao's star generals. In two fights both were slain, and Shao's army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 初，操壯關羽之為人，而察其心神無久留之意，使張遼以其情問之，羽歎曰：「吾極知曹公待我厚；

translations.literal: Earlier, Cao admired Yu's character, yet observed that his heart and spirit had no intention of staying long; he had Zhang Liao ask him of his intentions; Yu sighed and said, "I know full well Lord Cao treats me generously;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cao Cao admired Guan Yu's character but saw he would not stay. He had Zhang Liao sound him out. Guan Yu sighed and said, "I know well how generously Lord Cao treats me;

sentences.zh: 然吾受劉將軍恩，誓以共死，不可背之。

translations.literal: yet I received General Liu's kindness and swore to die together with him—I cannot betray him.
translations.idiomatic: yet I owe General Liu a deep debt and swore to live and die with him. I cannot betray him.

sentences.zh: 吾終不留，要當立效以報曹公乃去耳。

translations.literal: I will not remain in the end; I must when the time comes render service to repay Lord Cao and then leave.
translations.idiomatic: I will not stay forever. I must first repay Lord Cao with a deed of merit, and then go.

sentences.zh: 」遼以羽言報操，操義之，及羽殺顏良，操知其必去，重加賞賜。

translations.literal: " Liao reported Yu's words to Cao; Cao honored his righteousness; when Yu killed Yan Liang, Cao knew he would surely leave and added further rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao reported this to Cao Cao, who honored his loyalty. After Guan Yu killed Yan Liang, Cao Cao knew he would leave and heaped further honors on him.

sentences.zh: 羽盡封其所賜，拜書告辭，而奔劉備於袁軍。

translations.literal: Yu sealed up all he had been given, wrote a letter of farewell, and fled to Liu Bei in Shao's army.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu sealed up every gift he had received, wrote a letter of farewell, and rode off to Liu Bei in Yuan Shao's camp.

sentences.zh: 左右欲追之，操曰：「彼各為其主，勿追也。

translations.literal: Those around him wished to pursue; Cao said, "Each serves his own lord—do not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants wanted to give chase. Cao Cao said, "Each man serves his own lord. Let him go.

translations.literal: [closing quote]
translations.idiomatic: [closing quote]

sentences.zh: 操還軍官渡，閻柔遣使詣操，操以柔為烏桓校尉。

translations.literal: Cao returned his army to Guandu; Yan Rou sent an envoy to visit Cao, and Cao appointed Rou Colonel of the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao returned to Guandu. Yan Rou sent an envoy, and Cao Cao appointed him colonel of the Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 鮮于輔身見操於官渡，操以輔為右度遼將軍，還鎮幽土。

translations.literal: Xianyu Fu presented himself in person to Cao at Guandu; Cao appointed Fu General Who Crosses the Liao on the Right and sent him back to garrison the You region.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Fu came in person to Guandu. Cao Cao appointed him general who crosses the Liao on the right and sent him back to guard You province.

sentences.zh: 廣陵太守陳登治射陽，孫策西擊黃祖，登誘嚴白虎餘黨，圖為後害，策還擊登，軍到丹徒，須待運糧。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Guangling Chen Deng governed Sheyang; Sun Ce marched west to attack Huang Zu; Deng induced Yan Baihu's remaining followers and plotted to harm from behind; Ce turned back to attack Deng; the army reached Dantu and had to wait for grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng, administrator of Guangling, held Sheyang. Sun Ce was marching west against Huang Zu when Deng stirred up Yan Baihu's remnants to strike from the rear. Ce wheeled about to attack him. His army reached Dantu and halted to await supplies.

sentences.zh: 初，策殺吳郡太守許貢，貢奴客潛民間，欲為貢報仇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ce had killed the Administrator of Wu Commandery Xu Gong; Gong's servitor-guests lurked among the people, intending to avenge Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Ce had killed Xu Gong, the Wu commandery administrator. Gong's retainers hid among the people, plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 策性好獵，數出驅馳，所乘馬精駿，從騎絕不能及，卒遇貢客三人，射策中頰，後騎尋至，皆刺殺之。

translations.literal: Ce's nature loved hunting; he often went out driving and racing; the horse he rode was fine and swift and the following riders absolutely could not keep up; he suddenly encountered three of Gong's guests, who shot Ce in the cheek; the rear riders soon arrived and all were stabbed and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce loved the hunt and often rode out at speed on a superb horse, leaving his escort far behind. Three of Xu Gong's men ambushed him and shot him in the cheek. His escort caught up and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 策創甚，召張昭等謂曰：「中國方亂，以吳、越之眾，三江之固，足以觀成敗，公等善相吾弟！

translations.literal: Ce's wound was severe; he summoned Zhang Zhao and others and said, "The central realm is just now in disorder; with the hosts of Wu and Yue and the firmness of the Three Rivers, it is enough to watch success and failure—gentlemen, take good care of my younger brother!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce's wound was grave. He summoned Zhang Zhao and the others and said, "The heartland is in chaos. With the troops of Wu and Yue and the barrier of the Three Rivers, fortune can still be judged. Gentlemen, look after my brother!

sentences.zh: 」呼權，佩以印綬，謂曰：「舉江東之眾，決機於兩陳之間，與天下爭衡，卿不如我；

translations.literal: " He called Quan, hung the seal and cord on him, and said, "To command the hosts of the east of the river and decide at the moment between the two battle lines, contesting balance with the realm—you are not my equal;
translations.idiomatic: He called Sun Quan, invested him with seal and ribbon, and said, "In leading Jiangdong's armies and choosing the decisive stroke between battle lines, in competing with the realm—you are not my equal;

sentences.zh: 舉賢任能，各盡其心以保江東，我不如卿。

translations.literal: in raising the worthy and employing the able, each exhausting their heart to preserve the east of the river—I am not your equal.
translations.idiomatic: but in appointing the worthy and trusting men of talent, so that each gives his all to hold Jiangdong—I am not your equal.

sentences.zh: 」丙年，策卒，時年二十六。

translations.literal: " In the bingwu year, Ce died; at the time he was twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce died in the bingwu year, aged twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 權悲號，未視事，張昭曰：「孝廉，此寧哭時邪！

translations.literal: Quan wailed in grief and had not yet assumed office; Zhang Zhao said, "Filial and Incorrupt, is this really the time for weeping!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wailed and had not yet taken up his duties. Zhang Zhao said, "Young lord, is this a time for tears?

sentences.zh: 」乃改易權服，扶令上馬，使出巡軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he changed Quan's mourning garb, helped him mount a horse, and sent him out to inspect the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He changed Sun Quan's mourning dress, helped him onto a horse, and sent him out to review the army.

sentences.zh: 昭率僚屬，上表朝廷，下移屬城，中外將校，各令奉職，周瑜自巴丘將兵赴喪，遂留吳，以中護軍與張昭共掌眾事。

translations.literal: Zhao led the staff officials, submitted a memorial to the court, and issued orders down to the subject cities; commanders within and without were each ordered to perform their duties; Zhou Yu led troops from Baxiu to attend the funeral, then remained at Wu, and as Central Protector of the Army jointly managed all affairs with Zhang Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao led the staff, memorialized the court, and sent orders to every subject city; commanders at every level were told to hold their posts. Zhou Yu marched from Baxiu with troops for the funeral, then stayed at Wu, sharing command as Central Protector of the Army with Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 時策雖有會稽、吳郡、丹楊、豫章、廬江、廬陵，然深險之地，猶未盡從，流寓之士，皆以安危去就為意，未有君臣之固，而張昭、周瑜等謂權可與共成大業，遂委心而服事焉。

translations.literal: At the time, although Ce held Kuaiji, Wu Commandery, Danyang, Yuzhang, Lujiang, and Luling, yet in deeply perilous regions submission was not yet complete; guests and sojourners all took safety and danger as their guide to stay or leave, and there was not yet firmness between lord and minister—yet Zhang Zhao, Zhou Yu, and others judged that Quan could jointly accomplish the great enterprise, and so they devoted their hearts and served him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had held Kuaiji, Wu, Danyang, Yuzhang, Lujiang, and Luling, but the deep mountain country was not yet fully pacified. Wandering scholars weighed safety and flight; lord and subject bonds were still unsettled. Zhang Zhao, Zhou Yu, and others believed Sun Quan could carry the great work forward, and gave him their wholehearted service.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，立皇子馮為南陽王；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Emperor enfeoffed the imperial son Feng as Prince of Nanyang;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the emperor made his son Feng prince of Nanyang;

sentences.zh: 壬午，馮薨。

translations.literal: On the day rennwu, Feng died.
translations.idiomatic: On rennwu day Prince Feng died.

sentences.zh: 汝南黃巾劉辟等叛曹操應袁紹，紹遣劉備將兵助辟，郡縣多應之。

translations.literal: In Runan, the Yellow Turbans Liu Pi and others rebelled against Cao Cao to join Yuan Shao; Shao sent Liu Bei with troops to assist Pi, and many commanderies and counties responded.
translations.idiomatic: In Runan, Yellow Turban Liu Pi and others revolted against Cao Cao to support Yuan Shao. Shao dispatched Liu Bei with troops to aid Pi, and many districts rose with them.

sentences.zh: 紹遣使拜陽安都尉李通為征南將軍，劉表亦陰招之，通皆拒焉。

translations.literal: Shao sent envoys to appoint Yang'an Commandant Li Tong as General Who Suppresses the South; Liu Biao also secretly recruited him, but Tong refused both.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent envoys offering Li Tong, commandant of Yang'an, the title General Who Suppresses the South; Liu Biao also wooed him in secret. Tong turned them both down.

sentences.zh: 或勸通從紹，通按劍叱之曰：「曹公明哲，必定天下；

translations.literal: Some urged Tong to follow Shao; Tong grasped his sword and shouted rebuke, saying, "Lord Cao is wise and clear-sighted and will surely settle the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Tong to side with Shao. Tong gripped his sword and cried out: "Lord Cao is discerning and will unite the realm;

sentences.zh: 紹雖強盛，終為之虜耳。

translations.literal: Shao though strong and flourishing, in the end will become his captive.
translations.idiomatic: strong as Shao is, he will end as Cao's prisoner.

sentences.zh: 吾以死不貳。

translations.literal: I would rather die than serve two masters.
translations.idiomatic: I will die before I serve two masters.

sentences.zh: 」即斬紹使，送印綬詣操。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beheaded Shao's envoy and sent the seal and cord to Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Shao's envoy at once and delivered the seal and ribbon to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 通急錄戶調，朗陵長趙儼見通曰：「方今諸郡並叛，獨陽安懷附，復趣收其綿絹，小人樂亂，無乃不可乎？

translations.literal: Tong urgently registered household levies; Langling Prefect Zhao Yi saw Tong and said, "Just now all the commanderies are in rebellion; Yang'an alone holds loyal attachment—yet you again press to collect their silk and cotton; little men delight in disorder—would this not be inadvisable?
translations.idiomatic: Tong urgently pressed for household taxes. Langling magistrate Zhao Yi came to him and said, "Every district is in revolt while Yang'an alone stays loyal—yet you rush to seize their silk and cloth. Ordinary folk love turmoil; can this be wise?

sentences.zh: 」通曰：「公與袁紹相持甚急，左右郡縣背叛乃爾，若綿絹不調送，觀聽者必謂我顧望，有所須待也。

translations.literal: " Tong said, "The lord is locked in fierce stalemate with Yuan Shao; the neighboring commanderies and counties have rebelled to this extent—if silk and cotton are not assessed and delivered, observers will surely say I am wavering and waiting for some advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Tong said, "My lord is locked with Yuan Shao in a desperate standoff. Neighboring districts have already gone over. If I fail to deliver the silk levies, onlookers will say I am hedging my bets.

sentences.zh: 」儼曰：「誠亦如君慮，然當權其輕重。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "That is indeed as you consider, yet one must weigh light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "You have a point, but we must weigh priorities.

sentences.zh: 小緩調，當為君釋此患。

translations.literal: Ease the levy a little; I will relieve this trouble for you.
translations.idiomatic: Delay the levy slightly—I will clear this danger for you.

sentences.zh: 」乃書與荀彧曰：「今陽安郡百姓困窮，鄰城並叛，易用傾蕩，乃一方安危之機也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wrote to Xun Yu saying, "Now the people of Yang'an Commandery are exhausted and impoverished; neighboring cities have all rebelled and can easily be overturned—this is the pivot of safety and danger for a whole region.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Xun Yu: "The people of Yang'an are exhausted; neighboring cities have all rebelled and may topple at a touch. The safety of the whole region hangs on this.

sentences.zh: 且此郡人執守忠節，在險不貳，以為國家宜垂慰撫。

translations.literal: Moreover, the people of this commandery hold loyal integrity and in peril do not waver—I deem it fitting that the state should extend comfort and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: These people have stood firm in loyalty through danger. The state ought to reward that, not punish it.

sentences.zh: 而更急斂綿絹，何以勸善！

translations.literal: Yet instead you press urgently to gather silk and cotton—how can this encourage good conduct!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you squeeze them harder for silk and cotton—how does that encourage loyalty?

sentences.zh: 」彧即白操，悉以綿絹還民，上下歡喜，郡內遂安。

translations.literal: " Yu immediately reported to Cao, and all the silk and cotton was returned to the people; above and below rejoiced, and within the commandery there was peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu reported at once to Cao Cao, who returned every bolt to the people. High and low rejoiced, and the commandery settled.

sentences.zh: 通擊群賊瞿恭等，皆破之。

translations.literal: Tong attacked the bandits Qu Gong and others and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tong routed the bandit chiefs Qu Gong and the rest.

sentences.zh: 遂定淮、汝之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he settled the lands of Huai and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby pacified the Huai and Ru regions.

sentences.zh: 時操制新科，下州郡，頗增嚴峻，而調綿絹方急。

translations.literal: At the time Cao had enacted new statutes and sent them down to the commanderies and prefectures, greatly increasing severity, while the levy of silk and cotton was just then urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had just issued stern new laws to every commandery, even as the silk levy pressed hardest.

sentences.zh: 長廣太守何夔言於操曰：「先王辨九服之賦以殊遠近，制三典之刑以平治亂。

translations.literal: Changguang Administrator He Kui spoke to Cao, saying, "The ancient kings distinguished the levies of the nine domains to mark near and far, and established the three codes of punishment to balance order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Changguang administrator He Kui told Cao Cao: "The ancient kings graded tribute by distance and set three tiers of law to steady kingdoms in chaos or peace.

sentences.zh: 愚以為此郡宜依遠域新邦之典，其民間小事，使長吏臨時隨宜，上不背正法，下以順百姓之心。

translations.literal: I deem that this commandery ought to follow the precedents for distant borderlands and newly conquered states; as for small matters among the people, let the district officers temporarily act as circumstances require—above, not violating correct law; below, according with the hearts of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: This district should be governed like a distant frontier or new possession. Let local officers handle petty affairs as need arises—keeping to the law above while winning the people's trust below.

sentences.zh: 比及三年，民安其業，然後乃可齊之以法也。

translations.literal: By the time three years are reached, the people secure in their livelihoods, then one may align them with uniform law.
translations.idiomatic: Give the people three years to settle into their work, then apply the code evenly.

sentences.zh: 」操從之。

translations.literal: " Cao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 劉備略汝、穎之間，自許以南，吏民不安，曹操患之。

translations.literal: Liu Bei raided between the Ru and Ying rivers; south of Xu commandery, officials and people were unsettled—Cao was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei raided between the Ru and Ying; south of Xu, officials and commoners grew restless, and Cao Cao worried.

sentences.zh: 曹仁曰：「南方以大軍方有目前急，其勢不能相救，劉備以強兵臨之，其背叛故宜也。

translations.literal: Cao Ren said, "The south, because the great army just now has its present urgency, has no strength to send aid—the people turn against us when Liu Bei brings strong troops against them, and that is as it should be.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren said, "The south cannot be helped while our main force faces urgent business here. Liu Bei brings a strong army; rebellion is only natural.

sentences.zh: 備新將紹兵，未能得其用，擊之，可破也。

translations.literal: Bei has newly taken command of Shao's troops and has not yet been able to use them to full effect—attack him and he can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: He has only just taken Shao's troops and cannot yet wield them well. Strike now and we can break him.

sentences.zh: 」操乃使仁將騎擊備，破走之，盡復收諸叛縣而還。

translations.literal: " Cao thereupon sent Ren with cavalry to attack Bei, routed and drove him off, and fully recovered all the rebellious counties before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Ren with cavalry against Liu Bei, routed him, recaptured every rebel county, and returned.

sentences.zh: 備還至紹軍，陰欲離紹，乃說紹南連劉表。

translations.literal: Bei returned to Shao's army; secretly wishing to leave Shao, he urged Shao to link with Liu Biao in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei rejoined Shao's camp but wished to break away and urged Shao to ally with Liu Biao in the south.

sentences.zh: 紹遣備將本兵復至汝南，與賊龔都等合，眾數千人。

translations.literal: Shao sent Bei to lead his own troops again to Runan, where he joined with the bandits Gong Du and others—several thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Liu Bei back to Runan with his own troops; he joined bandit chief Gong Du and others, raising several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 曹操遣將蔡楊擊之，為備所殺。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent the general Cai Yang to attack him; he was killed by Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent General Cai Yang against him; Liu Bei killed him.

sentences.zh: 袁紹軍陽武，沮授說紹曰：「北兵雖眾而勁果不及南，南軍谷少而資儲不如北；

translations.literal: Yuan Shao's army was at Yangwu; Ju Shou urged Shao, saying, "Northern troops though numerous—their vigor and sharpness do not match the south's; southern troops have little grain and their stores do not match the north's;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao camped at Yangwu. Ju Shou urged him: "Your northern army is larger, but not as fierce as Cao's; Cao has less grain, but you are worse supplied;

sentences.zh: 南幸於急戰，北利在緩師。

translations.literal: the south thrives in urgent battle, the north profits in a drawn campaign.
translations.idiomatic: the south favors a quick fight, the north a war of attrition.

sentences.zh: 宜徐持久，曠以日月。

translations.literal: One ought to proceed slowly and endure long, letting months and days stretch out.
translations.idiomatic: Hold back and wear them down day by day.

sentences.zh: 」紹不從。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Shao refused.

sentences.zh: 八月，紹進營稍前，依沙堆為屯，東西數十里。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shao advanced his encampments slightly forward, relying on sand mounds for stockades, stretching east and west for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shao pushed his lines forward, building camps on sand knolls that stretched for miles east and west.

sentences.zh: 操亦分營與相當。

translations.literal: Cao also divided camps to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao matched him camp for camp.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day gengwu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day (gengwu), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 曹操出兵與袁紹戰，不勝，復還，堅壁。

translations.literal: Cao Cao went out with troops to battle Yuan Shao, did not win, returned again, and held firm behind walls.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched out to fight Yuan Shao, was defeated, withdrew, and dug in.

sentences.zh: 紹為高櫓，起土山，射營中，營中皆蒙楯而行。

translations.literal: Shao built lofty towers, raised earthen hills, and shot into the camp; within the camp all went shielded.
translations.idiomatic: Shao built towers and earthworks to rain arrows into Cao's camp; men moved only under shields.

sentences.zh: 操乃為霹靂車，發石以擊紹樓，皆破，紹復為地道攻操，操輒於內為長塹以拒之。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon made thunder carts, launching stones to strike Shao's towers—all were broken; Shao again made tunnels to attack Cao, and Cao repeatedly dug long trenches within to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao built catapults to smash Shao's towers, then dug counter-trenches when Shao tried mining.

sentences.zh: 操眾少糧盡，士卒疲乏，百姓困於徵賦，多叛歸紹者，操患之，與荀彧書，議欲還許，以致紹師。

translations.literal: Cao's host was few and grain exhausted; soldiers weary; the people distressed by levies—many rebelled and went over to Shao; Cao was troubled by this and wrote Xun Yu, discussing a wish to return to Xu to lure Shao's army away.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's army was dwindling and starving; his men were exhausted; heavy levies drove villagers to defect to Shao. Troubled, he wrote Xun Yu proposing retreat to Xu to draw Shao off.

sentences.zh: 彧報曰：「紹悉眾聚官渡，欲與公決勝敗。

translations.literal: Yu replied, saying, "Shao has gathered his whole host at Guandu and wishes to decide victory and defeat with you, lord.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu replied: "Shao has massed his full strength at Guandu to settle this with you.

sentences.zh: 公以至弱當至強，若不能制，必為所乘，是天下之大機也。

translations.literal: You with the utterly weak confront the utterly strong—if you cannot control him, you will surely be ridden by him; this is the great pivot of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: You are at your weakest facing his strongest. If you cannot master him here, he will master you—and the fate of the realm turns on it.

sentences.zh: 且紹，布衣之雄耳，能聚人而不能用。

translations.literal: Moreover Shao is a hero in plain cloth—able to gather men yet unable to use them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao is a mere commoner's champion: he can assemble men but not command them.

sentences.zh: 以公之神武明哲而輔以大順，何向而不濟！

translations.literal: With your divine martial prowess and clear wisdom, backed by the great mandate—toward what could you turn and not succeed!
translations.idiomatic: With your brilliance and the Mandate behind you, what could fail?

sentences.zh: 今谷食雖少，未若楚、漢在滎陽、成皋間也。

translations.literal: Now though grain is few, it is not yet like when Chu and Han were between Xingyang and Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: Grain is scarce, but not as scarce as when Liu Bang and Xiang Yu fought at Xingyang and Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 是時劉、項莫肯先退者，以為先退則勢屈也。

translations.literal: At that time Liu and Xiang would not consent to withdraw first, believing that whoever withdrew first would have his momentum bent.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Liu Bang nor Xiang Yu would yield first; each feared that retreat meant defeat.

sentences.zh: 公以十分居一之眾，畫地而守之，扼其喉而不得進，已半年矣。

translations.literal: You with one-tenth of the host, marking out ground and holding it, choking his throat so he cannot advance—it has already been half a year.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the line with one man for every ten of his, barring his throat for half a year already.

sentences.zh: 情見勢竭，必將有變。

translations.literal: Intent appears and momentum is exhausted—change will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit is broken and his strength spent—something must give.

sentences.zh: 此用奇之時，不可失也。

translations.literal: This is the hour to use the unorthodox—do not lose it.
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment for a daring stroke. Do not miss it.

sentences.zh: 」操從之，乃堅壁持之。

translations.literal: " Cao followed this and thereupon held firm behind walls and endured.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took his advice and dug in to wait.

sentences.zh: 操見運者，撫之曰：「卻十五日為汝破紹，不復勞汝矣。

translations.literal: When Cao saw the transport workers, he comforted them, saying, "In another fifteen days I will break Shao for you—you need not toil for me again.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting supply carriers, he told them, "In fifteen days I will break Shao for you—your labor ends soon.

sentences.zh: 」紹運谷車數千乘至官渡。

translations.literal: " Shao's grain carts, several thousand in number, reached Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's grain train—thousands of carts—reached Guandu.

sentences.zh: 荀攸言於操曰：「紹運車旦暮至，其將韓猛銳而輕敵。

translations.literal: Xun You spoke to Cao, saying, "Shao's transport carts will arrive at dawn or dusk; his general Han Meng is sharp and slighting toward the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You told Cao Cao: "Shao's grain carts will arrive any hour. His escort commander Han Meng is bold and careless.

sentences.zh: 擊，可破也！

translations.literal: Attack—and he can be broken!
translations.idiomatic: Hit him and you can break him!

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「誰可使者？

translations.literal: " Cao said, "Who can be sent?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked, "Who should go?

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「徐晃可。

translations.literal: " You said, "Xu Huang will do.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said, "Xu Huang.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣偏將軍河東徐晃與史渙邀擊猛，破走之，燒其輜重。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent Lieutenant General Xu Huang of Hedong and Shi Huan to intercept and strike Meng, routed and drove him off, and burned his baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lieutenant General Xu Huang of Hedong with Shi Huan to ambush Han Meng, routed him, and burned the supplies.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，紹復遣車運谷，使其將淳于瓊等將兵萬餘人送人，宿紹營北四十里。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Shao again sent carts to transport grain, ordering his generals Chunyu Qiong and others to lead more than ten thousand troops to escort them; they encamped forty li north of Shao's camp.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Shao sent another grain convoy under Chunyu Qiong and others with more than ten thousand men, camping forty li north of his main army.

sentences.zh: 沮授說紹：「可遣蔣奇別為支軍於表，以絕曹操之鈔。

translations.literal: Ju Shou urged Shao: "One could dispatch Jiang Qi to lead a separate force in a flanking position to cut off Cao Cao's raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou urged: "Send Jiang Qi with a separate force to block Cao's raiding parties.

sentences.zh: 」紹不從。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Shao refused.

sentences.zh: 許攸曰：「曹操兵少而悉師拒我，許下餘守，勢必空弱。

translations.literal: Xu You said, "Cao Cao's troops are few and he has marshaled his entire army to resist us; the remainder guarding Xu is bound to be empty and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Xu You said: "Cao Cao's army is small and his whole force blocks us here. Whatever guards Xu must be weak.

sentences.zh: 若分遣輕軍，星行掩襲，許可拔也。

translations.literal: If one dispatches light troops, marching like stars in a surprise raid, Xu can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Send light troops in a swift night raid and you can take Xu.

sentences.zh: 許拔，則奉迎天子以討操，操成禽矣。

translations.literal: If Xu is taken, then welcoming the Son of Heaven to crusade against Cao—Cao will become captive.
translations.idiomatic: Seize Xu, welcome the emperor, and march against Cao—and Cao is yours.

sentences.zh: 如其未潰，可令首尾奔命，破之必也。

translations.literal: If he has not yet collapsed, one can make front and rear run themselves ragged—in breaking him success is assured.
translations.idiomatic: If he does not fall at once, split his forces and harry him front and rear—you will surely break him.

sentences.zh: 」紹不從，曰：「吾要當先取操。

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow this, saying, "I must first take Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao refused: "I mean to finish Cao first.

sentences.zh: 」會攸家犯法，審配收系之，攸怒，遂奔操。

translations.literal: " Just then You's family violated the law; Shen Pei arrested and imprisoned them; You grew angry and thereupon fled to Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu You's family ran afoul of the law; Shen Pei had them arrested. Furious, Xu You defected to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操聞攸來，跣出迎之，撫掌笑曰：「子卿遠來，吾事濟矣！

translations.literal: When Cao heard You had come, he ran out barefoot to welcome him, clapping his hands and laughing, saying, "Ziqing has come from afar—my affair is saved!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Xu You had arrived, Cao Cao ran out barefoot to greet him, laughing and clapping: "Ziqing, you have come—my cause is saved!

sentences.zh: 」既入坐，謂操曰：「袁氏軍盛，何以待之？

translations.literal: " Once seated, he said to Cao, "Yuan Shi's army is flourishing—how do you propose to meet it?
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, Xu You asked: "Yuan Shao's army is vast. What is your plan?

sentences.zh: 今有幾糧乎？

translations.literal: How much grain do you have now?
translations.idiomatic: How much grain do you have?

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「尚可支一歲。

translations.literal: " Cao said, "It can still last a year.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Enough for a year.

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「無是，更言之！

translations.literal: " You said, "That is not so—say again!
translations.idiomatic: Xu You said, "Nonsense. Try again.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「可支半歲。

translations.literal: " He again said, "It can last half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Half a year, then.

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「足下不欲破袁氏邪！

translations.literal: " You said, "Do you not wish to break the Yuan clan!
translations.idiomatic: Xu You snapped: "Do you mean to defeat Yuan Shao or not?

sentences.zh: 何言之不實也！

translations.literal: Why speak untruthfully!
translations.idiomatic: Why lie to me?

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「向言戲之耳。

translations.literal: " Cao said, "What I said before was merely in jest.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed: "I was joking.

sentences.zh: 其實可一月，為之奈何？

translations.literal: In truth it can last a month—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: In truth, one month. What now?

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「公孤軍獨守，外無救援而糧谷已盡，此危急之日也。

translations.literal: " You said, "You, a lone army holding alone, with no rescue from without and grain already exhausted—this is the day of utmost peril.
translations.idiomatic: Xu You said: "You stand alone with no help coming and no grain left. This is the crisis hour.

sentences.zh: 袁氏輜重萬餘乘，在故市、烏巢，屯軍無嚴備，若以輕兵襲之，不意而至，燔其積聚，不過三日，袁氏自敗也。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan's baggage train of more than ten thousand carts is at Gushi and Wuchao; the garrison troops have no strict defense—if with light troops you raid them, arriving unanticipated, and burn their stored reserves, within no more than three days the Yuan clan will defeat itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's supply train—more than ten thousand carts—lies at Gushi and Wuchao, lightly guarded. Strike with a small force, take them unaware, burn the stores, and within three days Yuan Shao will destroy himself.

translations.literal: [closing quote]
translations.idiomatic: [closing quote]

sentences.zh: 操大喜，乃留曹洪、荀攸守營，自將步騎五千人，皆用袁軍旗幟，銜枚縛馬口，夜從間道出，人抱束薪，所歷道有問者，語之曰：「袁公恐曹操鈔略後軍，遣軍以益備。

translations.literal: Cao was greatly pleased; thereupon he left Cao Hong and Xun You to hold the camp, and personally led five thousand infantry and cavalry, all using Yuan army banners and pennants, with gags in their mouths and horses' mouths bound; by night they went out by a bypath, each man carrying a bundle of firewood; wherever they passed, if anyone asked, they were told, "Lord Yuan feared Cao Cao would raid and plunder the rear guard and dispatched troops to strengthen the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was delighted. He left Cao Hong and Xun You to hold camp and led five thousand foot and horse in Yuan banners, gags in their mouths and horses muffled. They slipped out by a hidden route at night, each man carrying kindling. When challenged on the road they said, "Lord Yuan fears Cao Cao may raid the rear and sent us to reinforce the depot.

sentences.zh: 」聞者信以為然，皆自若。

translations.literal: " Those who heard believed it true and all were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Believing them, the sentries never stirred.

sentences.zh: 既至，圍屯，大放火，營中驚亂。

translations.literal: Once arrived, they surrounded the depot and set great fires; within the camp there was alarm and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the depot, encircled it, and lit a great fire. The camp erupted in panic.

sentences.zh: 會明，瓊等望見操兵少，出陳門外，操急擊之，瓊退保營，操遂攻之。

translations.literal: At dawn, Qiong and the others saw that Cao's troops were few and came out to battle outside the camp gates; Cao urgently struck them; Qiong retreated to hold the camp, and Cao thereupon assaulted it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Chunyu Qiong saw how few Cao's men were and marched out to fight. Cao Cao struck hard; Qiong fell back into camp, and Cao pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 紹聞操擊瓊，謂其子譚曰：「就操破瓊，吾拔其營，彼固無所歸矣！

translations.literal: When Shao heard Cao was attacking Qiong, he said to his son Tan, "Even as Cao breaks Qiong, I will seize his camp—then he will have nowhere to return!
translations.idiomatic: Learning Cao Cao was attacking Qiong, Shao told his son Tan, "Let Cao break Qiong—I will take his camp and leave him nowhere to run!

sentences.zh: 」乃使其將高覽、張郃等攻操營。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent his generals Gao Lan and Zhang He and others to attack Cao's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gao Lan, Zhang He, and others to storm Cao Cao's camp.

sentences.zh: 郃曰：「曹公精兵往，必破瓊等，瓊等破，則事去矣，請先往救之。

translations.literal: He said, "Lord Cao's picked troops have gone—they will surely break Qiong and the others; when Qiong and the others are broken, the affair is lost—please let us first go to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He said: "Cao Cao's best troops are at Wuchao. They will break Qiong—and when Qiong falls, everything falls. Send us to relieve him first.

sentences.zh: 」郭圖固請攻操營。

translations.literal: " Guo Tu firmly urged attacking Cao's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu insisted on attacking Cao's camp instead.

sentences.zh: 郃曰：「曹公營固，攻之必不拔。

translations.literal: He said, "Lord Cao's camp is strong; attack it and it will surely not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He said: "Cao Cao's camp is solid. You cannot take it.

sentences.zh: 若瓊等見禽，吾屬盡為虜矣。

translations.literal: If Qiong and the others are captured, we all become prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: If Qiong is captured, we all become prisoners.

sentences.zh: 」紹但遣輕騎救瓊，而以重兵攻操營，不能下。

translations.literal: " Shao only sent light cavalry to rescue Qiong, while using heavy troops to attack Cao's camp—and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent only light cavalry to Wuchao and kept his main force hammering Cao's camp—which held.

sentences.zh: 紹騎至烏巢，操左右或言：「賊騎稍近，請分兵拒之。

translations.literal: Shao's cavalry reached Wuchao; someone among those at Cao's side said, "The rebel cavalry are drawing somewhat near—please divide troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's cavalry reached Wuchao. A staff officer warned Cao Cao: "Enemy horse are approaching—divide the force to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 」操怒曰：「賊在背後，乃白！

translations.literal: " Cao grew angry and said, "When the rebels are already behind you, then you report it!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao raged: "Tell me when they are on our backs, not before!

sentences.zh: 」士卒皆殊死戰，遂大破之，斬瓊等，盡燔其糧谷，殺士卒千餘人，皆取其鼻，牛馬割脣舌，以示紹軍，紹軍將士皆恟懼。

translations.literal: " The soldiers all fought to the death; thereupon they broke the enemy completely, beheaded Qiong and the others, burned all their grain, killed more than a thousand soldiers, took all their noses, and cut the lips and tongues of oxen and horses to display to Shao's army—Shao's army's officers and soldiers were all alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: His men fought like men with nothing left to lose. They smashed the depot, killed Qiong and his officers, burned every granary, slaughtered more than a thousand men, cut off their noses and the lips and tongues of cattle and horses, and displayed them to Shao's army. Panic spread through Shao's ranks.

sentences.zh: 郭圖慚其計之失，復譖張郃於紹曰：「郃快軍敗。

translations.literal: Guo Tu, ashamed that his plan had failed, again slandered Zhang He to Shao, saying, "He rejoices in our army's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu, shamed by his own bad counsel, again slandered Zhang He to Shao: "He is glad we lost.

sentences.zh: 」郃忿懼，遂與高覽焚攻具，詣操營降。

translations.literal: " He was both angry and fearful; thereupon he and Gao Lan burned the siege engines and went to Cao's camp to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged and afraid, Zhang He and Gao Lan burned their siege equipment and defected to Cao Cao's camp.

sentences.zh: 曹洪疑，不敢受，荀攸曰：「郃計畫不用，怒而來奔，君有何疑！

translations.literal: Cao Hong was suspicious and dared not accept them; Xun You said, "He's had his plans rejected and comes in anger to join us—what is there to doubt!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong hesitated to accept them. Xun You said: "Zhang He's counsel was ignored and he came here in rage—why doubt him?

sentences.zh: 」乃受之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong accepted the surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是紹軍驚擾，大潰，紹及譚等幅巾乘馬，與八百騎渡河。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shao's army was alarmed and thrown into disorder and routed completely; Shao and Tan and the others, wearing plain headcloths, mounted horses, and with eight hundred horsemen crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's army panicked and collapsed. Shao, Tan, and their companions tied plain cloths about their heads, mounted horses, and fled across the river with eight hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 操追之不及，盡收其輜重、圖書、珍寶。

translations.literal: Cao could not overtake them in pursuit and took all their baggage trains, maps and books, and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao could not catch them but seized every wagon train, archive, and treasure they left behind.

sentences.zh: 餘眾降者，操盡坑之，前後所殺七萬餘人。

translations.literal: Of the remaining masses who surrendered, Cao buried them all alive; in all, before and after, more than seventy thousand men were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrendered were buried alive. The dead numbered more than seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 沮授不及紹渡，為操軍所執，乃大呼曰：「授不降也，為所執耳！

translations.literal: Ju Shou did not reach Shao's crossing in time and was seized by Cao's army; he thereupon shouted loudly, saying, "Shou does not surrender—only captured!
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou failed to cross with Shao and was taken. He shouted: "I am not surrendering—I was captured!

sentences.zh: 」操與之有舊，迎謂曰：「分野殊異，遂用圮絕，不圖今日乃相禽也！

translations.literal: " Cao had old ties with him and went forward to meet him, saying, "We belong to different fates and so were severed—I never thought that today we would meet as captor and captive!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, who knew him of old, came forward: "Fortune set us in different realms and tore us apart—I never dreamed we would meet like this, hunter and hunted!

sentences.zh: 」授曰：「冀州失策，自取奔北。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "Ji Province was mismanaged—one brings defeat upon oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou replied: "Ji Province was mishandled. Shao brought this rout on himself.

sentences.zh: 授知力俱困，宜其見禽。

translations.literal: Shou's wisdom and strength were both exhausted—it was fitting that he should be captured.
translations.idiomatic: With his counsel and strength both spent, capture was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「本初無謀，不相用計，今喪亂未定，方當與君圖之。

translations.literal: " Cao said, "Benchu lacks strategy and did not employ your plans; now with defeat and disorder not yet settled, I am just about to consult with you on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said: "Benchu had no sense and ignored your plans. The realm is still unsettled—I mean to work this out with you.

sentences.zh: 」授曰：「叔父、母弟，縣命袁氏，若蒙公靈，速死為福。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "My uncle and younger brother born to my mother have their lives hanging with the Yuan clan—if I receive your grace, swift death would be a blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou said: "My kinsmen are bound to the Yuans. If you show mercy, let it be a quick death.

sentences.zh: 」操歎曰：「孤早相得，天下不足慮也。

translations.literal: " Cao sighed and said, "Had I gained you early, I would have no need to worry about the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sighed: "If I had had you from the first, the empire would hold no fears for me.

sentences.zh: 」遂赦而厚遇焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pardoned him and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He spared Ju Shou and treated him with honor.

sentences.zh: 授尋謀歸袁氏，操乃殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Shou plotted to return to the Yuan clan, and Cao thereupon executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shou soon tried to rejoin the Yuans. Cao Cao had him killed.

sentences.zh: 操收紹書中，得許下及軍中人書，皆焚之，曰：「當紹之強，孤猶不能自保，況眾人乎！

translations.literal: When Cao collected letters from Shao's belongings, he found correspondence from men in Xudu and from people in the army; he burned them all and said, "When Shao was strong, I could not even protect myself—how much less ordinary men!
translations.idiomatic: Among Shao's papers Cao Cao found letters from men in Xudu and from his own army. He burned them all. "When Shao was at his height I could barely save myself—who could blame the rest?

translations.literal: [closing quote]
translations.idiomatic: [closing quote]

sentences.zh: 冀州城邑多降於操。

translations.literal: Many fortified places in Ji Province submitted to Cao.
translations.idiomatic: City after city in Ji Province surrendered to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 袁紹走至黎陽北岸，入其將軍蔣義渠營，把其手曰：「孤以首領相付矣！

translations.literal: Yuan Shao fled to the north bank of the Liyang crossing and entered the camp of his general Jiang Yiqu; taking Yiqu's hand, he said, "I entrust my life and head to you!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao fled to the north bank of the Liyang ford and entered the camp of his general Jiang Yiqu. Taking Yiqu's hand, he said: "My life is in your hands!

sentences.zh: 」義渠避帳而處之，使宣號令。

translations.literal: " Yiqu moved aside from his own tent to house him and issued orders in his name.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu vacated his own tent for Shao and issued orders in his name.

sentences.zh: 眾聞紹在，稍復歸之。

translations.literal: When the masses heard Shao was there, they gradually returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops learned Shao was alive, they slowly rallied to him again.

sentences.zh: 或謂田豐曰：「君必見重矣。

translations.literal: Some told Tian Feng, "You will surely be held in high regard now.
translations.idiomatic: Some told Tian Feng: "Shao will honor you now.

sentences.zh: 」豐曰：「公貌寬而內忌，不亮吾忠，而吾數以至言迕之，若勝而喜，猶能赦我，今戰敗而恚，內忌將發，吾不望生。

translations.literal: " Feng said, "He looks broad-minded but harbors resentment within; he never saw my loyalty, and I often spoke blunt truth that offended him. Had we won and he were pleased, he might still have pardoned me. Now, defeated and enraged, that hidden spite will break out—I do not expect to live.
translations.idiomatic: Feng replied: "He looks generous but broods within. He never trusted my loyalty, and I spoke hard truth too often. Had we won, he might have spared me. Now, beaten and furious, his spite will surface—I do not expect to live.

sentences.zh: 」紹軍士皆拊膺泣曰：「向令田豐在此，必不至於敗。

translations.literal: " Shao's soldiers all beat their breasts and wept, saying, "If only Tian Feng had been here, we would never have come to this defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's soldiers beat their chests and wept: "If Tian Feng had been with us, we would never have lost like this.

sentences.zh: 」紹謂逄紀曰：「冀州諸人聞吾軍敗，皆當念吾，惟田別駕前諫止吾，與眾不同，吾亦慚之。

translations.literal: " Shao said to Pang Ji, "When the men of Ji Province hear our army was defeated, they will all think kindly of me—only Master Tian, as deputy director, previously warned me and stood apart from the crowd. I am ashamed of that too.
translations.idiomatic: Shao told Pang Ji: "When the men of Ji Province hear we were routed, they will pity me—except Tian Feng, who warned me before and stood alone against the rest. I am ashamed of that as well.

sentences.zh: 」紀曰：「豐聞將軍之退，拊手大笑，喜其言之中也。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "When Feng heard of the general's retreat, he clapped his hands and laughed greatly, pleased that his words had hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said: "When Feng heard of your retreat, he clapped his hands and laughed—delighted that his warning had come true.

sentences.zh: 」紹於是謂僚屬曰：「吾不用田豐言，果為所笑。

translations.literal: " Shao thereupon said to his staff, "I did not heed Tian Feng's words and have indeed been laughed at for it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then told his officers: "I ignored Tian Feng, and now he mocks me for it.

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he had Feng executed.
translations.idiomatic: He had Tian Feng executed.

sentences.zh: 初，曹操聞豐不從戎，喜曰：「紹必敗矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cao Cao heard Feng was not going on campaign, he rejoiced and said, "Shao is sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cao Cao learned Tian Feng was not joining the campaign, he rejoiced: "Shao is doomed.

sentences.zh: 」及紹奔遁，復曰：「向使紹用其別駕計，尚未可知也。

translations.literal: " When Shao fled in defeat, he said again, "Had Shao followed his deputy director's counsel, the outcome might still have been uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao fled in defeat, Cao Cao added: "Had Shao listened to his deputy director, the outcome might still be in doubt.

sentences.zh: 」審配二子為操所禽，紹將孟岱言於紹曰：「配在位專政，族大兵強，且二子在南，必懷反計。

translations.literal: " Shen Pei's two sons were captured by Cao. Shao's general Meng Dai said to Shao, "Pei holds power and monopolizes government; his clan is large and his troops strong, and with both sons in the south, he must harbor treasonous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei's two sons had been captured by Cao Cao. Shao's general Meng Dai warned him: "Pei monopolizes power, his clan is large and his army strong, and with both sons held in the south he must be plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 」郭圖、辛評亦以為然。

translations.literal: " Guo Tu and Xin Ping also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu and Xin Ping agreed.

sentences.zh: 紹遂以岱為監軍，代配守鄴。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon appointed Dai as army inspector to replace Pei in guarding Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shao made Meng Dai army inspector and sent him to hold Ye in Shen Pei's place.

sentences.zh: 護軍逄紀素與配不睦，紹以問之，紀曰：「配天性烈直，每慕古人之節，必不以二子在南為不義也。

translations.literal: Army Protector Pang Ji had long been on bad terms with Pei. Shao asked him about it. Ji said, "By nature Pei is fierce and upright; he always emulates the integrity of the ancients—he will surely not be disloyal simply because his two sons are in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Army Protector Pang Ji had long feuded with Shen Pei. Shao asked his view. Ji said: "Pei is fierce and upright by nature and models himself on the ancients—he would not turn traitor just because his sons are captive in the south.

sentences.zh: 願公勿疑。

translations.literal: I beg you, my lord, do not doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: Do not doubt him, my lord.

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「君不惡之邪？

translations.literal: " Shao said, "Do you not bear him ill will?
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked: "Do you not hate him?

sentences.zh: 」紀曰：「先所爭者，私情也；

translations.literal: " Ji said, "What we quarreled over before was private feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied: "What we quarreled over before was personal;

sentences.zh: 今所陳者，國事也。

translations.literal: what I now present is a matter of state.
translations.idiomatic: what I speak of now is the state's business.

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Shao said, "Well said!
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "Well said!

sentences.zh: 」乃不廢配，配由是更與紀親。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he did not remove Pei; Pei from this became closer with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shao kept Shen Pei in office, and Pei and Ji grew closer from that day.

sentences.zh: 冀州城邑叛紹者，紹稍復擊定之。

translations.literal: As for the fortified places in Ji Province that had rebelled against Shao, Shao gradually reconquered and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao gradually reconquered the Ji Province towns that had turned against him.

sentences.zh: 紹為人寬雅，有局度，喜怒不形於色，而性矜愎自高，短於從善，故至於敗。

translations.literal: Shao as a man was broad and refined, possessed of large-minded composure, and did not show joy or anger on his face—but by nature he was proud and stubborn, poor at accepting what was good, and so he came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was gracious and measured, never showing anger or delight on his face—but he was proud, stubborn, and slow to heed good counsel, and that was how he came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥，有星孛於大梁。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day xinhai, a comet appeared in Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day xinhai, a comet blazed in the Daliang constellation.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守李術攻殺揚州刺史嚴象，廬江梅乾、雷緒、陳蘭等各聚眾數萬在江淮間。

translations.literal: Li Shu, Administrator of Lujiang, attacked and killed Yan Xiang, Inspector of Yang Province; Mei Gan, Lei Xu, Chen Lan, and others of Lujiang each gathered multitudes numbering in the tens of thousands between the Yangtze and the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, Administrator of Lujiang, attacked and killed Yan Xiang, Inspector of Yang Province. Mei Gan, Lei Xu, Chen Lan, and others in Lujiang each raised armies of tens of thousands between the Yangtze and the Huai.

sentences.zh: 曹操表沛國劉馥為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Cao Cao memorialized recommending Liu Fu of Pei commandery as Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao recommended Liu Fu of Pei commandery as Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 時揚州獨有九江，馥單馬造合肥空城，建立州治，招懷乾、緒等，皆貢獻相繼。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Province held only Jiujiang. Fu came alone on horseback to the empty city of Hefei, established the provincial seat, and by conciliation and goodwill won over Gan, Xu, and the others—all sent tribute in steady succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province then held only Jiujiang. Fu rode alone into the empty city of Hefei, set up the provincial seat, and by conciliation won over Gan, Xu, and the rest—they sent tribute in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 數年中，恩化大行，流民歸者以萬數。

translations.literal: Within a few years his gracious rule spread widely, and displaced people who returned numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years his benevolent rule took hold, and displaced people returned by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 於是廣屯田，興陂堨；

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly expanded government farming and built dykes and embankments;
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded government farming and built dykes and embankments;

sentences.zh: 官民有畜，乃聚諸生，立學校；

translations.literal: when officials and people had stores in abundance, he gathered students and established schools;
translations.idiomatic: when officials and commoners had stores in hand, he gathered scholars and founded schools;

sentences.zh: 又高為城壘，多積木石，以修戰守之備。

translations.literal: and he raised the walls and ramparts high and stockpiled timber and stone to prepare for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: and he raised the walls high and stockpiled timber and stone for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 曹操聞孫策死，欲因喪伐之。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao heard Sun Ce had died, he wished to exploit the mourning period to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao heard Sun Ce was dead, he wanted to strike while the house of Sun was in mourning.

sentences.zh: 侍御史張紘諫曰：「乘人之喪，既非古義，若其不克，成仇棄好，不如因而厚之。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Counselor Zhang Hong admonished, saying, "Striking a man in his grief is not the way of antiquity. If you do not succeed, you will make an enemy and forfeit goodwill—it would be better to treat him generously instead.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Counselor Zhang Hong objected: "Attacking a house in mourning is not the way of antiquity. If you fail, you make an enemy and lose a friend—it is better to treat them generously instead.

sentences.zh: 」操即表權為討虜將軍，領會稽太守。

translations.literal: " Cao at once memorialized appointing Quan as General Who Exterminates Barbarians and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao at once recommended Sun Quan as General Who Exterminates Barbarians and Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 操欲令紘輔權內附，及以紘為會稽東部都尉。

translations.literal: Cao wanted Hong to assist Quan in submitting inwardly, and also appointed Hong Eastern Commandant of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wanted Zhang Hong to help bring Sun Quan into the fold, and appointed Hong Eastern Commandant of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 紘至吳，太夫人以權年少，委紘與張昭共輔之。

translations.literal: When Hong reached Wu, the Dowager Lady, seeing Quan was young, entrusted Hong and Zhang Zhao together to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hong reached Wu, the Dowager Lady, seeing Sun Quan was still young, entrusted him and Zhang Zhao to assist him together.

sentences.zh: 紘惟補察，知無不為。

translations.literal: Hong devoted himself to oversight and correction; there was nothing he knew of that he did not act on.
translations.idiomatic: Hong devoted himself to oversight and remedy; nothing came to his attention that he did not act on.

sentences.zh: 太夫人問揚武都尉會稽董襲曰：「江東可保不？

translations.literal: The Dowager Lady asked Yangwu Commandant Dong Xi of Kuaiji, "Can the lands east of the Yangtze be held?
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager Lady asked Yangwu Commandant Dong Xi of Kuaiji: "Can we hold the lands east of the Yangtze?

sentences.zh: 」襲曰：「江東有山川之固，而討逆明府恩德在民，討虜承基，大小用命，張昭秉眾事，襲等為爪牙，此地利人和之時也，萬無所憂。

translations.literal: " Xi said, "East of the Yangtze has the strength of mountains and rivers; the late Lord Who Quelled Rebellion left his grace among the people; Lord Who Exterminates Barbarians inherits the foundation—all, great and small, obey orders; Zhang Zhao handles the affairs of the multitude; Xi and the rest serve as claws and fangs—this is a time when terrain and hearts align. There is absolutely nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Xi replied: "East of the Yangtze has mountains and rivers for its ramparts. The late Lord Who Quelled Rebellion left his grace among the people; Lord Who Exterminates Barbarians inherits his foundation—all, high and low, obey. Zhang Zhao handles the multitude's affairs; Xi and the rest serve as claws and fangs. Terrain and hearts are with us. There is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」權遺張紘之部，或以紘本受北任，嫌其志趣不止於此，權不以介意。

translations.literal: " When Quan sent Zhang Hong to his post, some, knowing Hong had originally been entrusted by the north, suspected his ambitions did not end there—but Quan did not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan sent Zhang Hong to his post, some, knowing Hong had been sent from the north, suspected his ambitions ran further—but Quan took no offense.

sentences.zh: 魯肅將北還，周瑜止之，因薦肅於權曰：「肅才宜佐時，當廣求其比以成功業。

translations.literal: Lu Su was about to return north; Zhou Yu stopped him and recommended Su to Quan, saying, "Su's talent suits the needs of the age. You should widely seek his like to achieve the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su was about to return north; Zhou Yu stopped him and recommended him to Sun Quan: "Su's talent fits the age. Seek out more like him if you mean to build a great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 」權即見肅，與語，悅之。

translations.literal: " Quan at once received Su and spoke with him, and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan received Lu Su at once, spoke with him, and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 賓退，獨引肅合榻對飲，曰：「今漢室傾危，孤思有桓、文之功，君何以佐之？

translations.literal: When the guests withdrew, he alone drew Su to share a couch and drink facing each other, saying, "The House of Han now totters—I aspire to the achievement of Duke Huan and Duke Wen. How will you assist me?
translations.idiomatic: When the guests had gone, he drew Lu Su alone to share a couch and drink with him face to face. "The House of Han is failing," he said. "I aspire to the achievement of Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi and Jin. How will you help me?

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「昔高帝欲尊事義帝而不獲者，以項羽為害也。

translations.literal: " Su said, "In the past the High Emperor wished to honor and serve Emperor Yi but could not achieve it because Xiang Yu stood in the way.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su said: "The High Emperor wished to honor Emperor Yi but could not, because Xiang Yu blocked him.

sentences.zh: 今之曹操，猶昔項羽，將軍何由得為桓、文乎！

translations.literal: Today's Cao Cao is like the Xiang Yu of old—how can the general become a Duke Huan or Duke Wen!
translations.idiomatic: Today's Cao Cao is yesterday's Xiang Yu—how can you become a Duke Huan or Duke Wen!

sentences.zh: 肅竊料之，漢室不可復興，曹操不可卒除，為將軍計，惟有保守江東以觀天下之釁耳。

translations.literal: Su privately judged that the House of Han could not be revived, Cao Cao could not be swiftly removed—for the general's planning, there was only to hold Jiangdong and watch for openings in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Su judged privately that Han cannot be restored and Cao Cao cannot be removed quickly. For you, the only course is to hold Jiangdong and watch for openings in the realm.

sentences.zh: 若因北方多務，剿除黃祖，進伐劉表，竟長江所極，據而有之，此王業也。

translations.literal: If, taking advantage of the north's many affairs, you eliminate Huang Zu, advance to attack Liu Biao, reach the end of the Yangtze, seize and hold it—this would be royal foundation.
translations.idiomatic: If, while the north is busy, you eliminate Huang Zu, advance against Liu Biao, and hold the Yangtze to its end—that is the foundation of kingship.

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「今盡力一方，冀以輔漢耳，此言非所及也。

translations.literal: " Quan said, "For now I exert all my strength in one region, hoping to support Han—this talk is beyond what I can reach.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said: "For now I mean to do all I can in one corner, hoping to support Han—that vision is beyond me.

sentences.zh: 」張昭毀肅年少粗疏，權益貴重之，賞賜儲偫，富擬其舊。

translations.literal: " Zhang Zhao disparaged Su as young and crude, but Quan valued him all the more, granting rewards and stored provisions until his wealth matched what he had before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao dismissed Lu Su as young and careless, but Sun Quan valued him all the more, rewarding him until his wealth matched what he had before.

sentences.zh: 權料諸小將兵少而用薄者，併合之。

translations.literal: Quan reckoned out the junior generals whose troops were few and stipends thin and merged their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan consolidated the commands of junior generals whose troops were few and pay was thin.

sentences.zh: 別部司馬汝南呂蒙，軍容鮮整，士卒練習。

translations.literal: Separate-division Marshal Lü Meng of Runan—his army's appearance was fresh and orderly, his soldiers well drilled.
translations.idiomatic: Separate-division Marshal Lü Meng of Runan kept his troops trim and his soldiers well drilled.

sentences.zh: 權大悅，增其兵，寵任之。

translations.literal: Quan was greatly pleased, increased his troops, and favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was greatly pleased, increased his command, and favored him with trust.

sentences.zh: 功曹駱統勸權尊賢接士，勤求損益，饗賜之日，人人別進，問其燥濕，加以密意，誘諭使言，察其志趣。

translations.literal: Records Officer Luo Tong urged Quan to honor the worthy and receive scholars, diligently seeking what could be improved. On days of feasting and reward, he had each man come forward separately, asked after his health and comfort, added intimate goodwill, encouraged and instructed them to speak, and observed their inclinations.
translations.idiomatic: Records Officer Luo Tong urged Sun Quan to honor the worthy and receive scholars, and to seek constant improvement. On feast days he had each man come forward alone, asked after his health and comfort, spoke to him with private warmth, drew out his views, and watched his inclinations.

sentences.zh: 權納用焉。

translations.literal: Quan adopted and applied this.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan adopted the practice.

sentences.zh: 統，俊之子也。

translations.literal: Tong was the son of Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong was the son of Luo Jun.

sentences.zh: 廬陵太守孫輔恐權不能保江東，陰遣人繼書呼曹操。

translations.literal: Sun Fu, Administrator of Luling, feared Quan could not hold Jiangdong and secretly sent messengers repeatedly with letters summoning Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu, Administrator of Luling, feared Sun Quan could not hold Jiangdong and secretly sent repeated messages summoning Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 行人以告，權悉斬輔親近，分其部曲，徙輔置東。

translations.literal: When travelers reported this, Quan executed all of Fu's close associates, divided his command, and moved Fu to the east.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Sun Quan, he executed all of Sun Fu's close associates, divided his troops, and moved Fu eastward.

sentences.zh: 曹操表徵華歆為議郎、參司空軍事。

translations.literal: Cao Cao memorialized summoning Hua Xin as Gentlemen Consultant and Participant in the Affairs of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao recommended summoning Hua Xin as Gentlemen Consultant and staff officer to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守李術不肯事權，而多納其亡叛。

translations.literal: Li Shu, Administrator of Lujiang, refused to serve Quan and took in many of his deserters and fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, Administrator of Lujiang, refused to serve Sun Quan and sheltered many of his deserters.

sentences.zh: 權以狀白曹操曰：「嚴刺史昔為公所用，而李術害之，肆其無道，宜速誅滅。

translations.literal: Quan reported the facts to Cao Cao, saying, "Inspector Yan was once employed by you, yet Li Shu killed him, indulging his lawlessness—he should swiftly be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan reported the matter to Cao Cao: "Inspector Yan once served you, yet Li Shu killed him in open defiance of law. He should be destroyed at once.

sentences.zh: 今術必復詭說求救。

translations.literal: Now Shu will surely again employ deceitful pleas to seek rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Shu will surely plead for rescue with more deceitful words.

sentences.zh: 明公居阿衡之任，海內所瞻，願敕執事，勿復聽受。

translations.literal: My lord holds the charge of the royal assistant—all under Heaven look to you. I beg you to instruct your officers not to heed such appeals again.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the charge of the royal assistant and all the realm looks to you. I beg you to instruct your officers not to listen.

sentences.zh: 」因舉兵攻術於皖城。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he raised troops and attacked Shu at Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Then he raised troops and attacked Li Shu at Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 術求救於操，操不救。

translations.literal: Shu sought rescue from Cao; Cao did not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu begged Cao Cao for help; Cao Cao did not come.

sentences.zh: 遂屠其城，梟術首。

translations.literal: Thereupon the city was sacked, and Shu's head was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The city was sacked and Li Shu's head was displayed.

sentences.zh: 徙其部曲二萬餘人。

translations.literal: More than twenty thousand of his troops were relocated.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand of his troops were relocated.

sentences.zh: 劉表攻張羨，連年不下。

translations.literal: Liu Biao attacked Zhang Xian and for years could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao besieged Zhang Xian for years without success.

sentences.zh: 曹操方與袁紹相拒，未暇救之。

translations.literal: Cao Cao was just then locked in confrontation with Yuan Shao and had no leisure to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was locked in confrontation with Yuan Shao and had no time to intervene.

sentences.zh: 羨病死，長沙復立其子懌。

translations.literal: Xian died of illness; Changsha again enthroned his son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian died of illness; Changsha enthroned his son Yi in his place.

sentences.zh: 表攻懌及零、桂，皆平之。

translations.literal: Biao attacked Yi and Lingling and Gui commanderies and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao attacked Yi and pacified Lingling and Gui commanderies.

sentences.zh: 於是表地方數千里，帶甲十餘萬，遂不供職貢，郊祀天地，居處服用，僭擬乘輿焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Biao's territory stretched several thousand li; he fielded more than a hundred thousand armored troops. He ceased sending tribute, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, and in dwelling, dress, and equipage usurped the trappings of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao now held territory thousands of li across and more than a hundred thousand armored men. He stopped sending tribute, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, and in dwelling, dress, and equipage took on the trappings of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 張魯以劉璋暗懦，不復承順，襲別部司馬張修，殺之而並其眾。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu, finding Liu Zhang dark-minded and weak, no longer obeying, attacked Separate-division Marshal Zhang Xiu, killed him, and absorbed his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu, finding Liu Zhang timid and weak, stopped obeying him, attacked Separate-division Marshal Zhang Xiu, killed him, and absorbed his troops.

sentences.zh: 璋怒，殺魯母及弟，魯遂據漢中，與璋為敵。

translations.literal: Zhang was furious and killed Lu's mother and younger brother; Lu then held Hanzhong and became Zhang's enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang was furious and killed Lu's mother and brother. Lu seized Hanzhong and made himself Zhang's enemy.

sentences.zh: 璋遣中郎將龐羲擊之，不克。

translations.literal: Zhang sent General of the Household Pang Xi to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang sent General of the Household Pang Xi against him but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 璋以羲為巴郡太守，屯閬中以御魯。

translations.literal: Zhang made Xi Administrator of Ba commandery and stationed him at Langzhong to guard against Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang made Pang Xi Administrator of Ba commandery and stationed him at Langzhong to hold Zhang Lu at bay.

sentences.zh: 羲輒召漢昌賨民為兵，或構羲於璋，璋疑之。

translations.literal: Xi repeatedly conscripted Cong tribesmen of Hanchang as soldiers; some slandered Xi to Zhang, and Zhang grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xi repeatedly conscripted Cong tribesmen of Hanchang as soldiers. Some slandered him to Liu Zhang, and Zhang grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 趙韙數諫不從，亦恚恨。

translations.literal: Zhao Wei repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded and also harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wei remonstrated again and again without being heeded and nursed his own resentment.

sentences.zh: 初，南陽、三輔民流入益州者數萬家，劉焉悉收以為兵，名曰東州兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, people from Nanyang and the Three Metropolises who had fled into Yizhou numbered tens of thousands of households; Liu Yan took them all as soldiers and called them Eastern Province Troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, tens of thousands of households from Nanyang and the Three Metropolises had fled into Yizhou. Liu Yan enrolled them all as soldiers and called them the Eastern Province Troops.

sentences.zh: 璋性寬柔，無威略，東州人侵暴舊民，璋不能禁。

translations.literal: Zhang was by nature lenient and mild, without martial authority; Eastern Province men plundered the old inhabitants, and Zhang could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang was lenient and mild, without force of command. Eastern Province men preyed on the old inhabitants, and he could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 趙韙素得人心，因益州士民之怨，遂作亂，引兵數萬攻璋；

translations.literal: Zhao Wei had long won hearts among the people; taking advantage of the resentment of Yizhou's gentry and commoners, he thereupon raised rebellion and led tens of thousands of troops to attack Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wei had long held the people's hearts. Riding the resentment of Yizhou's gentry and commoners, he rebelled and led tens of thousands of troops against Liu Zhang;

sentences.zh: 厚賂荊州，與之連和。

translations.literal: he lavishly bribed Jing Province and joined forces with it.
